docs.text:
# Core API Usage

The `null-graph` core package owns the WebGPU device, render passes, compute stages, batches, and
buffer streaming. This page covers the main `NullGraph` engine surface; see
[Deprecated API](../deprecated-api.md) if you are migrating from an older version.

> **Going lower level?** For the bind-group conventions, the instance-data layout, the `Camera`
> uniform (WGSL struct + offsets), the full `ComputeStageConfig`, and the `BufferManager` /
> `TextureManager` / `engine.ctx` surfaces, see the
> [Core Reference](./core-reference.md).

## Engine Initialization

```ts
import { NullGraph, Camera } from 'null-graph';

const engine = new NullGraph();
const result = await engine.init(canvas, {
    desiredFeatures: ['timestamp-query'],   // extra optional features, negotiated against the adapter
    powerPreference: 'high-performance',    // 'high-performance' (default) | 'low-power'
    autoNegotiate: true,                    // default: opportunistically enable modern features
    // width / height override — useful with an OffscreenCanvas
});

if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.error);
```

`canvas` may be an `HTMLCanvasElement` **or** an `OffscreenCanvas`, so the whole engine can run in a
Web Worker — **or `null`**, see below. After init you can read `engine.width` / `engine.height`,
reach shared GPU resources via `engine.ctx` (e.g. `engine.ctx.cameraUniformBuffer`), and access
`engine.device`, `engine.bufferManager`, `engine.textureManager`, and `engine.capabilities`.

## Headless rendering & sharing a device

Two options change *where* the engine runs rather than how it renders. Both are additive — a
canvas-only `init(canvas)` behaves exactly as before.

**No canvas — `init(null, { width, height })`.** The main-screen pass renders into an offscreen
texture, `engine.screenTexture` (`RENDER_ATTACHMENT | COPY_SRC`, format `engine.ctx.format`:
`'rgba8unorm'` unless you pass `format`). This is how the engine runs in Node (Dawn), in tests, and
in the render-to-PNG tool. `width` and `height` are required — there is no canvas to size from —
and `engine.resize(w, h)` recreates the screen texture. `engine.ctx.isHeadless` tells the two apart.

```ts
const engine = new NullGraph();
await engine.init(null, { width: 512, height: 512 });
// ...build passes; a pass with isMainScreenPass: true draws into engine.screenTexture
engine.render(sequence);
// copyTextureToBuffer(engine.screenTexture) to read the frame — in a test, never in the frame loop
```

**Adopt a device — `init(canvas | null, { device })`.** Use a `GPUDevice` another library already
created instead of requesting one, so the two share buffers with no copy. The motivating case is
ONNX Runtime Web: create the session first (ORT owns the device), then adopt it, and bind a model
output's `tensor.gpuBuffer` directly in a compute stage.

```ts
import * as ort from 'onnxruntime-web/webgpu';

const session = await ort.InferenceSession.create(model, {
    executionProviders: ['webgpu'], preferredOutputLocation: 'gpu-buffer',
});
await engine.init(canvas, { device: await ort.env.webgpu.device });

const { output } = await session.run({ input });              // stays on the GPU
engine.setComputePassBindGroup(stage, [{ binding: 0, resource: { buffer: output.gpuBuffer } }, /* … */]);
engine.render([stage, scenePass]);
await engine.device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone();               // keep the tensor alive until read…
output.dispose();                                              // …then release it
```

- Adopt in that direction (the runtime owns, NullGraph adopts): the runtime requests the features
  and limits its kernels need, and NullGraph's baseline needs no optional feature. ONNX Runtime
  1.29 allows no other: given a device the app made, its runs fail.
- **ONNX Runtime destroys its device with its last session.** Keep a session alive while the
  engine renders on that device, or use `OrtRuntime` from `null-graph/inference`, which keeps one
  for its whole life and runs models over the engine's buffers
  ([inference.md](./inference.md#onnx-runtime)).
- Nothing is negotiated on an adopted device. `engine.capabilities` reports what it already has
  (subgroup sizes from `device.adapterInfo` where the browser exposes it); `powerPreference` and
  `autoNegotiate` are refused with a named error, and a missing `desiredFeatures` entry warns.
- `engine.ctx.ownsDevice` is `false`, and NullGraph never destroys a device it adopted.
- **`engine.destroy()` releases what the engine created, and only that.** That covers:
  - its batches' own buffers — never a `sharedSourceBuffer`, geometry, or a `cameraBuffer` you passed;
  - the texture manager's textures;
  - the screen and depth targets and the camera uniform;
  - the canvas's configuration;
  - the device, only if the engine requested it.

  `render()` then does nothing. Destroy extras first (`PostChain`, `LightSystem`, …): they own
  their resources. Idempotent, and safe after a failed `init`; every release is attempted and
  failures are thrown together. Destroying an engine's own device rejects reads still pending on
  it, so await `device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone()` first if something is reading back.
- Pipelines and shader modules carry labels — a batch's `label` (default `"<pass> #<index>"`) and a
  compute stage's `name` — so a WebGPU validation error names what caused it.

Executable versions of both: `test/core-gpu` (C1–C6) and `test/onnx-gpu` (O1–O3), run by
`npm run test:gpu`.

## Feature Negotiation & Capabilities

To stay in sync with WebGPU's progression, `init()` **opportunistically enables** a curated set of
forward-looking features whenever the adapter supports them — currently `subgroups`, `shader-f16`,
`bgra8unorm-storage`, and `dual-source-blending` (`PROGRESSION_FEATURES`). This is purely additive:
every candidate is checked against the adapter's support list first, so it can only ever *enable* an
optional capability, never fail init. Set `autoNegotiate: false` to request only your explicit
`desiredFeatures`.

It also raises three **limits** to the adapter's own values (`PROGRESSION_LIMITS`):
`maxStorageBuffersPerShaderStage`, `maxStorageBufferBindingSize` and `maxBufferSize`. Without
that, a device gets WebGPU's defaults whatever the GPU offers: 8 storage buffers per stage and
128 MB bindings, where current desktop GPUs report 16 and about 2 GB. The list is curated, not
"every limit", because the spec warns that better limits can cost performance on some
implementations. Read the result on `engine.device.limits`. Modules size against those limits and
refuse above them with a named error, so code that needs more than the defaults fails loudly on a
baseline device. `autoNegotiate: false` gives a device with the defaults, which is how to check
that an app runs on the baseline. An adopted device keeps the limits its owner chose.

The negotiated result is exposed as `engine.capabilities` — a structured, queryable snapshot the
engine uses internally (e.g. the clustered `LightSystem` switches to a subgroup-accelerated binning
kernel when `capabilities.subgroups` is set) and that you can read for your own code paths:

```ts
const caps = engine.capabilities; // GPUCapabilities

caps.subgroups;           // boolean — subgroup ops (enable subgroups;) available
caps.shaderF16;           // boolean — 16-bit floats (enable f16;) available
caps.bgra8unormStorage;   // boolean — bgra8unorm usable as a storage texture
caps.dualSourceBlending;  // boolean — @blend_src(0/1) available
caps.subgroupMinSize;     // number  — hardware subgroup size range (0 if unsupported)
caps.subgroupMaxSize;     // number
caps.has('timestamp-query'); // membership test against the enabled feature set
caps.features;            // ReadonlySet<GPUFeatureName> — everything the device granted
```

> The `shaderF16`, `bgra8unormStorage`, and `dualSourceBlending` flags are detected as **groundwork**
> — they are surfaced now so those features can be adopted later without re-plumbing negotiation.

## Render Passes
NullGraph isolates rendering logic into distinct passes. You can render pristine 3D scenes offscreen and pipe them into post-processing passes.

```ts
// 1. Create an offscreen pass
const scenePass = engine.createPass({
    name: 'Offscreen Pass',
    isMainScreenPass: false,
    colorAttachments: [{
        view: offscreenTexture.createView(),
        clearValue: { r: 0.0, g: 0.01, b: 0.03, a: 1.0 },
        loadOp: 'clear', storeOp: 'store'
    }],
    // ... depth attachments
});

// 2. Create the final Post-Processing pass
const hudPass = engine.createPass({
    name: 'HUD Post Process',
    isMainScreenPass: true
});

// 3. Bind the offscreen texture to your post-process batch
const hudBatch = engine.createBatch(hudPass, { /* shader args */ });
engine.createTextureBindGroup(hudBatch, offscreenTexture.createView(), sampler);
```

**A main-screen pass always clears to `(0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 1)`** (1.2.1, `RenderPipeline`). The engine replaces its
attachments with the screen's, so any `colorAttachments` or `clearValue` it was given are ignored. For another
background, clear an offscreen pass of your own (a post chain's scene attachments are one), or draw a fullscreen
batch first.

## Indirect Drawing (GPU Compute Culling)
Stop relying on the CPU to figure out what to render. A **compute stage** evaluates thousands of
instances, writes an `IndirectDrawArgs` buffer, and commands the vertex shader without the CPU ever
knowing what happened.

> **Changed:** compute is no longer embedded in a batch via `computeShaderCode`. Create a standalone
> `ComputeStageNode` with `engine.createComputeStage(...)` and sequence it explicitly in `render()`.
> See [Deprecated API §2](../deprecated-api.md) for the migration.

```ts
// 1. An indirect batch allocates its indirect + source buffers (no pipeline)
const batch = engine.createBatch(scenePass, {
    isIndirect: true,
    shaderCode: renderShaderCode,
    strideFloats: 14,
    maxInstances: 5000,
    vertexLayouts: geometry.layout.getWebGPUDescriptor(),
});

// 2. A separate compute stage does the culling and writes drawArgs
const cull = engine.createComputeStage({
    name: 'Frustum Cull',
    shaderCode: cullWGSL, // atomicAdd(&drawArgs.instanceCount, 1u); ... cull & pack
    dispatchCount: [Math.ceil(5000 / 64), 1, 1],
    preClearBuffers: [
        { buffer: batch.indirectBuffer!, offset: 4, data: new Uint32Array([0]) },
    ],
});

engine.setComputePassBindGroup(cull, [
    { binding: 0, resource: { buffer: engine.ctx.cameraUniformBuffer } },
    { binding: 1, resource: { buffer: batch.sourceStorageBuffer! } },
    { binding: 2, resource: { buffer: batch.storageBuffer } },
    { binding: 3, resource: { buffer: batch.indirectBuffer! } },
], 0);

// 3. Execute compute first, then the draw pass
engine.render([cull, scenePass]);
```

## Advanced Alpha Blending
Whether you need standard transparency or intense additive glowing effects, NullGraph exposes WebGPU's blend states directly at the batch level.

```ts
// Example: Additive Blending for a particle system (Quantum Nebula)
const physicsBatch = engine.createBatch(scenePass, {
    // ... shaders and layout configs
    
    // ADDITIVE BLENDING: Colors sum together, creating intense glowing cores
    blend: {
        color: { srcFactor: 'src-alpha', dstFactor: 'one', operation: 'add' },
        alpha: { srcFactor: 'one', dstFactor: 'one', operation: 'add' }
    },
    depthWriteEnabled: false,
    depthCompare: 'less'
});
```

## Streaming Instance Data (Zero-Copy)
Batches are backed by a pre-allocated storage buffer. Blast a flat `Float32Array` — computed on the
main thread or in a Web Worker — straight into it. The default instance stride is 14 floats
(index/pad, position xyz, rotation quat xyzw, scale xyz, color rgb).

```ts
engine.setBatchGeometry(batch, geom.vertexBuffer!, geom.indexBuffer!, geom.indices.length);

const data = new Float32Array(instanceCount * 14);
// ... fill per-instance transforms ...
engine.updateBatchData(batch, data, instanceCount);
```

## Custom Bind Groups
Attach arbitrary resources to a batch's render pipeline (materials, skeletons, light buffers). For
compute stages, use the compute variant.

```ts
// Render pipeline (default group index 1)
engine.setRenderPassBindGroup(batch, [
    { binding: 0, resource: { buffer: skeletonManager.boneBuffer } },
], 2);

// Compute stage (default group index 0)
engine.setComputePassBindGroup(computeStage, entries, 0);
```

## Execution
`render()` accepts an explicit, ordered sequence of compute stages and render passes — the modern,
Data-Oriented path. Called with no arguments it replays every tracked pass in creation order.

```ts
engine.updateCamera(camera);            // upload camera uniforms (432-byte block)
engine.render([cullStage, scenePass, postPass]); // explicit order
// engine.render();                     // legacy: replays all createPass() nodes
```

## Camera & resource managers

A core `Camera` produces the view/projection matrices the engine uploads; `engine.bufferManager` and
`engine.textureManager` create geometry buffers and load/generate textures.

```ts
import { Camera } from 'null-graph';

const camera = new Camera(75, canvas.width / canvas.height, 0.1, 1000);
camera.updateView([0, 3, 8], [0, 0, 0]); // eye, target
engine.updateCamera(camera);

// Geometry buffers from raw typed arrays
const vbo = engine.bufferManager.createVertexBuffer(vertices);
const ibo = engine.bufferManager.createIndexBuffer(indices);

// Textures (sRGB TRUE for albedo/color, FALSE for normal/data maps)
const albedo = await engine.textureManager.load('/albedo.png', { sRGB: true });
```

Full signatures — the `Camera` methods, the WGSL camera struct, and every `BufferManager` /
`TextureManager` member — are in the [Core Reference](./core-reference.md).

## Cheat sheet

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `init(canvas, options)` | Boot WebGPU; returns `{ success, enabledFeatures, error? }`. |
| `init(null, { width, height })` | Boot headless — the main pass renders into `engine.screenTexture`. |
| `init(canvas \| null, { device })` | Adopt an existing device (e.g. ONNX Runtime's) instead of requesting one. |
| `resize(w, h)` | Reallocate the depth texture (and the headless screen texture) for a new size. |
| `createPass(config)` | Create a render pass (screen or offscreen). |
| `removePass(pass)` | (1.2.1) Forget a pass: `render()` without a sequence stops drawing it. Its batches stay: `clearBatch` them first. True when the engine held it. |
| `createBatch(pass, config)` | Create a render batch (pipeline + storage buffer). |
| `createBatchAsync(pass, config)` | (1.2.1) The same batch, its pipeline from `createRenderPipelineAsync`: frames go on while it compiles, so a world rebuilds without freezing the one on screen. Nothing is allocated and the pass is untouched until the pipeline exists. A shader that does not compile rejects, naming the batch, with the device's message about the WGSL; so does an engine destroyed during the compile. |
| `clearBatch(pass, batch)` | Remove a batch from its pass and free the buffers the engine allocated for it (never a caller's shared buffer). |
| `createComputeStage(config)` | Create a standalone GPU compute stage. |
| `createComputeStageAsync(config)` | The same stage, its pipeline from `createComputePipelineAsync`: the compile does not hold the caller. A shader that does not compile rejects, naming the stage, with the device's message about the WGSL. |
| `removeComputeStage(stage)` | (1.2.1) Forget a stage. The engine holds every stage it makes until `destroy()`; a world that replaces its stages removes the old ones so their pipelines can be collected. A sequence that still lists the stage still runs it. True when the engine held it. |
| `setBatchGeometry(batch, vb, ib, count, format?)` | Bind vertex/index buffers to a batch. |
| `updateBatchData(batch, data, count)` | Stream instance data into a batch (Zero-Copy). |
| `createTextureBindGroup(batch, views, sampler, extra?, group?)` | Build/cache a texture bind group. |
| `setRenderPassBindGroup(batch, entries, group?)` | Bind custom resources to a batch. |
| `setComputePassBindGroup(stage, entries, group?)` | Bind custom resources to a compute stage. |
| `updateCamera(camera)` | Upload the camera uniform block. |
| `render(sequence?)` | Execute the pipeline. |
| `destroy()` | Release what the engine created (batch buffers it allocated, textures, targets, camera uniform, canvas configuration; its device only if it requested it). `render()` does nothing afterwards. |

**Engine properties:** `device`, `ctx` (readonly `WebGPUContext`), `capabilities` (readonly
`GPUCapabilities`), `bufferManager`, `textureManager`, `width`, `height`, `isDestroyed`,
`screenTexture` (headless only), `canvas` (`null` when headless). On `ctx`: `isHeadless`,
`ownsDevice`, `getScreenView()`, and `context` (`undefined` when headless). See the
[Core Reference](./core-reference.md#7-the-shared-context-enginectx).

docs.title: Core Reference
docs.text:
# Core Reference

The low-level companion to the [Core API guide](./core.md). It documents the pieces you reach for
when writing custom shaders or wiring resources by hand: the **bind-group conventions** the engine
assumes, the **instance data layout**, the **`Camera`** uniform, **`ComputeStageConfig`** in full,
and the two resource managers (`BufferManager`, `TextureManager`) plus the shared context
(`engine.ctx`).

Read [core.md](./core.md) first for the high-level engine flow.

---

## 1. Bind-group conventions

Every shader NullGraph runs shares the same group layout. If you write custom WGSL, match it — the
engine binds these groups for you and a mismatch throws at bind-group creation.

| Group | Binding | Resource | Bound by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0** | 0 | `camera` uniform (432-byte block) | `createBatch` (automatic) |
| **0** | 1 | instance **storage buffer** (`array<...>`, `strideFloats` per instance) | `createBatch` (automatic) |
| **1** | 0… | material params + textures/samplers | `createTextureBindGroup` / `setRenderPassBindGroup` / a `Material` |
| **2** | 0… | lights (and cluster grid/indices) | `LightSystem.applyToBatch` |

- **Group 0** is filled automatically for every batch: binding 0 is the global camera uniform,
  binding 1 is the batch's own instance storage buffer (what `updateBatchData` streams into).
- **Group 1** is the conventional "material" slot. The material classes and
  `createTextureBindGroup` default to group index 1.
- **Group 2** is the conventional "lights" slot (`LightSystem.applyToBatch` defaults to it).

Compute stages are independent: `setComputePassBindGroup` defaults to **group 0**, and you declare
whatever bindings your kernel needs.

---

## 2. Instance data layout

Each batch owns one pre-allocated storage buffer of `maxInstances * strideFloats * 4` bytes.
`updateBatchData(batch, data, count)` streams a flat `Float32Array` into it (Zero-Copy), and the
vertex shader indexes it by `@builtin(instance_index)`.

The stock shader builders assume a **14-float stride**:

| Float offset | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | index / pad | free slot (the builders start reading at 1) |
| 1, 2, 3 | position | world XYZ |
| 4, 5, 6, 7 | rotation | quaternion XYZW |
| 8, 9, 10 | scale | XYZ |
| 11, 12, 13 | color | RGB |

```wgsl
// How the built-in vertex shaders read it:
let base = iIdx * 14u;
let ecsPos   = vec3<f32>(ecs[base + 1u], ecs[base + 2u], ecs[base + 3u]);
let ecsRot   = vec4<f32>(ecs[base + 4u], ecs[base + 5u], ecs[base + 6u], ecs[base + 7u]);
let ecsScale = vec3<f32>(ecs[base + 8u], ecs[base + 9u], ecs[base + 10u]);
```

```ts
// Populate one instance
const data = new Float32Array(14);
data[1] = x; data[2] = y; data[3] = z;   // position
data[7] = 1.0;                            // rotation quat W (identity)
data[8] = data[9] = data[10] = 1.0;       // scale
data[11] = 0.1; data[12] = 0.5; data[13] = 0.9; // color
engine.updateBatchData(batch, data, 1);
```

`strideFloats` is per-batch and fully custom — set it to whatever your own shader reads (post-process
passes use `8`, for example). The 14-float layout is only a convention the material builders adopt.

---

## 3. `Camera`

```ts
import { Camera } from 'null-graph';

const camera = new Camera(
    75,                              // fovDegrees
    canvas.width / canvas.height,    // aspect
    0.1,                             // near
    1000.0,                          // far
);
```

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `updateView(eye, target, up?)` | Recompute view + inverse-view and the combined matrices. `up` defaults to `[0,1,0]`. |
| `updateProjection(aspect)` | Recompute projection + inverse-projection (call on resize / aspect change). |
| `updateTime(simTime)` | Write a time value into the uniform's padding slot (float 99) — drives GPU animation (e.g. `EmissiveMaterial` pulse). |

Public fields include `fovDegrees`, `near`, `far`, the matrices, and `bufferData` (108 floats /
432 bytes — the contiguous block `engine.updateCamera` uploads).

### The Camera uniform (WGSL)

Custom shaders declare this struct at `@group(0) @binding(0)`. It matches `Camera.bufferData`
byte-for-byte:

```wgsl
struct Camera {
    viewProj:    mat4x4f,  // 0
    view:        mat4x4f,  // 16
    proj:        mat4x4f,  // 32
    invViewProj: mat4x4f,  // 48
    invView:     mat4x4f,  // 64
    invProj:     mat4x4f,  // 80
    eye:         vec3f,    // 96  (eye position)
    time:        f32,      // 99  (updateTime writes here)
    near:        f32,      // 100
    far:         f32,      // 101
    fovRads:     f32,      // 102
    aspect:      f32,      // 103
    _padEnd:     vec4f,    // 104–107 (reserved)
};
@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> camera: Camera;
```

> The inverse matrices exist for World-space reconstruction (SSR, decals, SSAO), billboarding, and
> clustered light culling. See [Deprecated API §3](../deprecated-api.md) for the migration note if you
> maintained a shader against the old 20-float camera.

### Frame usage

```ts
function frame() {
    const t = performance.now() * 0.001;
    camera.updateTime(t);
    camera.updateView([Math.sin(t) * 8, 3, Math.cos(t) * 8], [0, 0, 0]);
    engine.updateCamera(camera);   // uploads the 432-byte block
    engine.render([scenePass]);
    requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}

// On canvas resize:
engine.resize(w, h);
camera.updateProjection(w / h);
```

---

## 4. `ComputeStageConfig`

`engine.createComputeStage(config)` builds a standalone `ComputeStageNode`. The kernel's entry point
must be `cs_main`.

```ts
const stage = engine.createComputeStage({
    name: 'My Compute',
    shaderCode: myWGSL,                 // must define @compute fn cs_main(...)
    dispatchCount: [64, 1, 1],          // static, OR a function (see below)
    workgroupSize: [64, 1, 1],          // read by nothing in 1.2.1: the WGSL's @workgroup_size decides
    preClearBuffers: [
        { buffer: counterBuffer, offset: 0, data: new Uint32Array([0]) },
    ],
});
```

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | Debug label. |
| `shaderCode` | `string` | WGSL; entry point `cs_main`. |
| `dispatchCount` | `[x,y,z]` **or** `() => [x,y,z]` | Workgroup counts. A function is re-evaluated each frame — use it for size-dependent dispatch (e.g. tied to canvas resolution). |
| `workgroupSize` | `[x,y,z]` | Accepted, and read by nothing in 1.2.1: the `@workgroup_size(...)` in the WGSL alone sets the size. Size `dispatchCount` from that. |
| `preClearBuffers` | `BufferClearConfig[]` | Buffer resets run **immediately before** the dispatch, every frame. |

`BufferClearConfig` = `{ buffer: GPUBuffer, offset: number, data: Uint32Array | Float32Array }`.

The dynamic-dispatch form is why culling stages can react to a resize without recompiling:

```ts
dispatchCount: () => [Math.ceil(engine.width / 8), Math.ceil(engine.height / 8), 1],
```

Bind resources with `engine.setComputePassBindGroup(stage, entries, groupIndex = 0)`, then include
the stage in the `render(...)` sequence **before** whatever consumes its output. See
[Indirect Drawing](./core.md#indirect-drawing-gpu-compute-culling) and the
[Lights compute reference](./lights-shader-reference.md#4-rolling-your-own-compute-stage-over-the-light-buffers).

---

## 5. `BufferManager` (`engine.bufferManager`)

Thin helpers that create GPU buffers from typed arrays, mapped at creation (no staging copy).

```ts
const vbo = engine.bufferManager.createVertexBuffer(float32Vertices); // VERTEX | COPY_DST
const ibo = engine.bufferManager.createIndexBuffer(uint16OrUint32Indices); // INDEX | COPY_DST
engine.setBatchGeometry(batch, vbo, ibo, indices.length, 'uint16');
```

| Method | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `createVertexBuffer(data: Float32Array)` | `GPUBuffer` | Vertex usage; sized to `data.byteLength`. |
| `createIndexBuffer(data: Uint16Array \| Uint32Array)` | `GPUBuffer` | Index usage; size rounded up to 4-byte alignment. Pass the matching `'uint16'`/`'uint32'` format to `setBatchGeometry`. |

(The [`Geometry`](./geometry.md) class wraps these behind `upload(engine)` — use the manager
directly when you have raw arrays, e.g. from `GeometryBuilder.build()` or a GLB parser.)

---

## 6. `TextureManager` (`engine.textureManager`)

Loads, decodes, caches, and generates textures, and hands out samplers. Cached by URL + color space,
so loading the same texture twice is free.

```ts
// Albedo/color maps: sRGB TRUE (GPU linearizes on sample).
const albedo = await engine.textureManager.load('/tex/albedo.png', { sRGB: true });
// Normal / ARM / data maps: sRGB FALSE.
const normal = await engine.textureManager.load('/tex/normal.png', { sRGB: false });
```

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `load(url, { sRGB?, samplerDescriptor? })` | Fetch → decode → upload → cached `GPUTextureView`. Falls back to a 1×1 white texture on failure. |
| `getSampler(descriptor)` | Cached `GPUSampler` (keyed by stringified descriptor). |
| `getSolidTexture(r, g, b, a?)` | 1×1 solid-color `GPUTextureView` (0–255 per channel), cached. |
| `fallbackWhite` | 1×1 white — default albedo/packed fallback. |
| `fallbackNormal` | 1×1 `(128,128,255)` — flat tangent-space normal. |
| `defaultSampler` | Linear filtering, `repeat` addressing — good default for 3D models. |
| `clearCache()` | Destroy all cached textures and drop samplers (call when tearing down a scene). |

> **`sRGB` matters.** Pass `true` only for color/albedo maps. Passing it for normal/roughness/metallic
> maps corrupts the data by applying gamma to values that aren't colors.

The materials system leans on `fallbackWhite` / `fallbackNormal` whenever a texture option is
omitted — see [Materials](./materials.md#how-materials-work).

---

## 7. The shared context (`engine.ctx`)

`engine.ctx` is the `WebGPUContext` — a `public readonly` surface for the low-level resources the
engine allocates. Reach for it when a custom compute stage or shader needs a shared buffer.

| Member | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ctx.device` | `GPUDevice` | Same object as `engine.device`. |
| `ctx.format` | `GPUTextureFormat` | Swapchain format (may be `*-srgb`). |
| `ctx.cameraUniformBuffer` | `GPUBuffer` | The 432-byte global camera uniform — bind it into compute stages. |
| `ctx.depthTexture` | `GPUTexture` | Engine depth attachment (`depth24plus`, `RENDER_ATTACHMENT` only — not samplable). |
| `ctx.width` / `ctx.height` | `number` | Current drawing-buffer size (also `engine.width` / `engine.height`). |
| `ctx.destroy()` / `ctx.isDestroyed` | method / `boolean` | Releases the targets, the camera uniform and the canvas configuration, and the device only when `ctx.ownsDevice`; `engine.destroy()` calls it. |

> `ctx.depthTexture` is render-attachment only. For a **samplable** scene depth (e.g. SSAO), declare
> `gbuffer.depth` on a [`PostChain`](./post.md), which allocates a separate sampled depth target.

docs.title: Debug UI API Usage
Deprecated & Breaking API Changes
docs.text:
# Deprecated & Breaking API Changes

This document tracks APIs that have been **renamed**, **removed**, or **restructured** in
NullGraph, along with drop-in migration steps. Entries are derived from the diff between the
last published surface and the current `src/` tree.

> NullGraph follows a "brutalist" philosophy: when an API stops reflecting the underlying
> data model, it is renamed rather than aliased. There are **no silent shims** — the old
> names are gone, so update call sites directly using the tables below.

---

## 1. Bind-group API renamed (`null-graph` core)

The bind-group helpers on `NullGraph` were renamed to say what they actually do (they build
and cache a `GPUBindGroup`), and the render/compute paths were split into two explicit methods.

### `attachTextureMaterial()` → `createTextureBindGroup()`

Same signature, same return value. Only the name changed.

```ts
// ❌ Before
const bg = engine.attachTextureMaterial(batch, [albedoView, normalView], sampler, extra, 1);

// ✅ After
const bg = engine.createTextureBindGroup(batch, [albedoView, normalView], sampler, extra, 1);
```

> Note: `StandardPBRMaterial` already calls the new method internally — if you only use the
> material classes you don't need to change anything.

### `attachCustomBindGroup()` → `setRenderPassBindGroup()` / `setComputePassBindGroup()`

The old method took a `target: 'render' | 'compute' | 'both'` argument because batches used to
own an embedded compute pipeline. Compute is now a **standalone stage** (see §2), so the method
was split so each target has a dedicated call.

| Old call | New call |
|---|---|
| `attachCustomBindGroup(batch, entries, group)` (default `'render'`) | `setRenderPassBindGroup(batch, entries, group)` |
| `attachCustomBindGroup(batch, entries, group, 'compute')` | `setComputePassBindGroup(stage, entries, group)` |
| `attachCustomBindGroup(batch, entries, group, 'both')` | Call both methods explicitly |

```ts
// ❌ Before — bound to the batch's hidden compute pipeline
engine.attachCustomBindGroup(meshBatch, entries, 2, 'render');

// ✅ After — render binding goes to the batch...
engine.setRenderPassBindGroup(meshBatch, entries, 2);

// ...and compute binding goes to a ComputeStageNode (default group index is 0)
engine.setComputePassBindGroup(computeStage, entries, 0);
```

---

## 2. Compute is no longer embedded in a batch (breaking)

Previously you enabled GPU-driven rendering by passing `computeShaderCode` into `createBatch`,
and the batch silently created and dispatched a compute pipeline. That coupling is removed.
Compute now lives in a **separate, explicit `ComputeStageNode`** that you sequence yourself.

**Removed from `PipelineConfig`:**

- `computeShaderCode`
- `extraBindGroup`

**Removed from `RenderBatch`:**

- `computePipeline`
- `computeBindGroup`
- `computeCustomBindGroups`

**New API:** `engine.createComputeStage(config)`, `engine.setComputePassBindGroup(stage, ...)`,
and an explicit `render(pipelineSequence)` sequence (see §4).

```ts
// ❌ Before — one batch that hid a compute cull pass
const batch = engine.createBatch(pass, {
    isIndirect: true,
    computeShaderCode: cullWGSL,
    shaderCode: drawWGSL,
    strideFloats: 14,
    maxInstances: 5000,
});
engine.render(); // compute ran implicitly

// ✅ After — create the indirect batch first, then a separate compute stage
const batch = engine.createBatch(pass, {
    isIndirect: true,
    shaderCode: drawWGSL,
    strideFloats: 14,
    maxInstances: 5000,
    sharedSourceBuffer: sourceBuffer, // instance data the compute stage reads/writes
});

const cull = engine.createComputeStage({
    name: 'Frustum Cull',
    shaderCode: cullWGSL,
    dispatchCount: [Math.ceil(5000 / 64), 1, 1],
    preClearBuffers: [
        { buffer: batch.indirectBuffer!, offset: 4, data: new Uint32Array([0]) }, // reset instanceCount
    ],
});

engine.setComputePassBindGroup(cull, [
    { binding: 0, resource: { buffer: engine.ctx.cameraUniformBuffer } },
    { binding: 1, resource: { buffer: sourceBuffer } },
    { binding: 2, resource: { buffer: batch.storageBuffer } },
    { binding: 3, resource: { buffer: batch.indirectBuffer! } },
], 0);

// Explicit ordering: compute first, then the pass that draws its results
engine.render([cull, pass]);
```

When `isIndirect: true`, `createBatch` still allocates `indirectBuffer` and (if you don't pass
`sharedSourceBuffer`) a `sourceStorageBuffer` for you — it just no longer builds the pipeline.

---

## 3. Camera uniform layout changed (breaking for custom WGSL)

The camera uniform buffer was expanded from **20 floats (80 bytes)** to **108 floats (432 bytes)**
to carry view/projection **inverse** matrices (for SSR, decals, clustered culling, billboarding)
plus scalar metadata. If you wrote your own WGSL `Camera` struct, it must be updated.

| Data | Old offset (floats) | New offset (floats) |
|---|---|---|
| `viewProj` (mat4) | 0 | 0 |
| `view` (mat4) | — | 16 |
| `proj` (mat4) | — | 32 |
| `invViewProj` (mat4) | — | 48 |
| `invView` (mat4) | — | 64 |
| `invProj` (mat4) | — | 80 |
| **`eyePosition` (vec3)** | **16** | **96** |
| time (padding slot, via `camera.updateTime`) | — | 99 |
| `zNear`, `zFar`, `fovRads`, `aspect` | — | 100–103 |

The largest breaking change is that **`eyePosition` moved from float offset 16 to 96**. Any
hand-written shader that read the eye position at the old location will now read a matrix row.
The stock shader builders (`buildPBRShader`, etc.) already reference the new `Camera` struct —
only fully custom shaders are affected. See the canonical struct in `src/core/Camera.ts`.

`updateCamera()` now writes `camera.bufferData.byteLength` (432 bytes) instead of a hardcoded
`20 * 4`, so no call-site change is needed as long as you use the `Camera` class.

---

## 4. `render()` takes an explicit pipeline sequence

`render()` still works with no arguments (it replays every tracked pass in creation order — the
legacy path). The modern, data-oriented path is to pass an **explicit ordered array** of compute
stages and render passes, which is required for GPU-driven culling and post-processing.

```ts
// ✅ Legacy (still supported): replays all createPass() nodes in order
engine.render();

// ✅ Modern: you control the exact execution order, including compute
engine.render([lightBinningStage, cullStage, scenePass, postPass]);
```

---

## 5. `init()` signature widened

`WebGPUContext.init(canvas, desiredFeatures[])` became `init(canvas, options)`. At the
`NullGraph` level, `init(canvas, { desiredFeatures })` still works, and the options object now
also accepts `powerPreference`, `width`, and `height`, and the canvas may be an `OffscreenCanvas`.

```ts
// ✅ Still valid
await engine.init(canvas, { desiredFeatures: ['timestamp-query'] });

// ✅ New options
await engine.init(offscreenCanvas, {
    desiredFeatures: ['timestamp-query'],
    powerPreference: 'high-performance',
    width: 1920,
    height: 1080,
});
```

---

## 6. Engine context is now public: `gpuCtx` → `ctx`

The engine's WebGPU context was a private field named `gpuCtx`. It is now exposed as a
`public readonly ctx` so you can reach shared resources (notably
`engine.ctx.cameraUniformBuffer`) when wiring custom compute stages. If you were reaching into
the private `gpuCtx` via a cast, switch to the supported `engine.ctx`.

```ts
// ❌ Before (unsupported internal access)
const camBuf = (engine as any).gpuCtx.cameraUniformBuffer;

// ✅ After
const camBuf = engine.ctx.cameraUniformBuffer;
```

New convenience getters `engine.width` and `engine.height` are also available.

---

## 7. Materials module: `ShaderBuilder.ts` → `PBRShaderBuilder.ts`

The file `src/extras/materials/ShaderBuilder.ts` was renamed to `PBRShaderBuilder.ts`. The
exported function name is **unchanged** (`buildPBRShader`), and the public subpath is still
`null-graph/materials`, so the standard import keeps working:

```ts
// ✅ Unchanged — import from the module, not the file
import { buildPBRShader, StandardPBRMaterial } from 'null-graph/materials';
```

Only breaks if you deep-imported the file path directly (e.g. `null-graph/materials/ShaderBuilder`),
which was never a supported entry point. The materials module now also ships `buildBasicShader`,
`buildLambertShader`, `buildToonShader`, `buildEmissiveShader`, and `buildMatcapShader` alongside
their matching material classes.

---

## 8. Feature negotiation is now automatic (`engine.capabilities`)

`init()` now **opportunistically enables** a curated set of modern WebGPU features when the adapter
supports them (`subgroups`, `shader-f16`, `bgra8unorm-storage`, `dual-source-blending`), in addition
to any `desiredFeatures` you pass. This is additive — each candidate is guarded against the adapter's
support list, so it only ever *enables* an optional feature and can never make init fail.

Two consequences to be aware of:

- `result.enabledFeatures` (and `device.features`) may now list features you did not explicitly
  request. Opt out with `init(canvas, { autoNegotiate: false })` for the old request-only behavior.
- The negotiated set is exposed as `engine.capabilities` (a `GPUCapabilities` snapshot). The clustered
  `LightSystem` reads `capabilities.subgroups` to select a subgroup-accelerated binning kernel; on
  hardware without the feature it uses the identical-output atomic baseline, so there is **no API or
  output change** — only a faster path where available.

```ts
// Opt out of auto-negotiation (request only what you list)
await engine.init(canvas, { desiredFeatures: ['timestamp-query'], autoNegotiate: false });

// Read what was negotiated
if (engine.capabilities.subgroups) { /* pick a subgroup code path */ }
```

No call-site changes are required; existing `init()` calls keep working.

---

## 9. `VisibilitySystem.getCullStage()` → `getCullStages()` (visibility, 2026-10-16)

The instance tier now culls in two compute stages per draw batch (visibility-design §14):
1. a **cull** that records visibility bits and block counts;
2. a **scatter** that writes the survivors **in source order**, with no global atomic.

The draw order is therefore the same every frame and every run. Overlapping instances no longer
change which one wins a depth tie, and offline films are bit-exact. Since a batch now has more than
one stage, the getter returns them all, in order.

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `getCullStage(batch): ComputeStageNode` or `null` | `getCullStages(batch): ComputeStageNode[]`: the batch's cull and scatter, in order. `[]` for a batch the system did not create. The meshlet tier returns its one stage. |
| `buildInstanceCullWGSL(opts)` wrote survivors with `atomicAdd` | Same name and options; it is now the first stage (bits and block counts). `buildInstanceScatterWGSL()` is the second. |
| At most 65,535 × 64 = 4,194,240 instances culled per draw | At most 65,535 × 256 = 16,776,960 (`INSTANCE_CULL_GROUP` = 256). A larger `maxInstances` is refused by name. |

```ts
// ❌ Before
const stage = vis.getCullStage(batch);
if (stage) stage.enabled = active;

// ✅ After: gate, or run, every stage of the batch, in order
for (const stage of vis.getCullStages(batch)) stage.enabled = active;
```

The library's own callers (ShadowSystem, ProbeVolume, Picker) are updated. The meshlet tier still
compacts with `atomicAdd` (visibility-design §14.4, phase 2).

---

*Have a migration that isn't covered here? Open an issue on the
[NullGraph repository](https://github.com/Vikas593-cloud/NullGraph).*

docs.title: Environment API Usage
docs.text:
# Environment API Usage

The `null-graph/environment` module is the indirect-lighting runtime. It replaces the constant that
currently stands in for the *entire* indirect term in the PBR fragment —

```wgsl
let ambient = vec3<f32>(0.3) * albedo * ao;   // what you get without this module
```

— with the split-sum image-based lighting model: a **GGX-prefiltered environment cube** for
specular, an **SH-L2 projection** for diffuse, and a **BRDF integration LUT** to join them.

The load-bearing idea (design §5): indirect lighting is a **sibling contract** to direct lighting.
`LightSystem.getShaderLayout()` injects `getVisibleLightCount` / `getIncidentLight`;
`EnvironmentSystem.getShaderLayout()` injects `getIndirectDiffuse` / `getIndirectSpecular`. Both are
`{ wgslStructs, wgslLogic }` pairs composed into the material by the same mechanism, so **no
material file knows either one exists**.

- **Architecture:** [`lighting-ibl-design.md`](../lighting-ibl-design.md)
- **Buffer layouts, WGSL contracts, the material bridge:** [`environment-shader-reference.md`](./environment-shader-reference.md)

## 1. What you can build with this

Phase 1 gives you **one environment for the whole scene**, from any of three sources, plus the sky
that matches it. That covers more than it sounds like — here is the honest range.

### 1.1 The zero-asset outdoor scene

A procedural gradient sky with a sun disc. No HDR file, no download, no asset pipeline.

```ts
const env = new EnvironmentSystem(engine, {});
env.setProceduralSky({
    zenith:  [0.10, 0.22, 0.52],   // linear HDR, not sRGB
    horizon: [0.65, 0.72, 0.85],
    ground:  [0.28, 0.24, 0.20],
    sunDir:  [-0.4, -1.0, -0.35],  // TRAVEL direction: where the light GOES
    sunIntensity: 18,
});
```

The sun disc in the source cube is what makes the prefiltered specular have a real highlight and
the SH have a dominant direction. Turn `sunIntensity` up and the whole scene keys off it.

**Point the `LightSystem`'s directional light along the same `sunDir`** and the direct and indirect
halves agree. For a static scene, storing that direction once is enough. For an animated sun, use
[`TimeOfDay`](./time-of-day.md): it writes one computed direction into the sky, direct-light,
shadow, and exposure contracts so those copies cannot drift.

### 1.2 A photographed environment (HDR / LDR equirect)

```ts
await env.setEquirect('/hdr/sunset_2k.hdr');       // linear data
await env.setEquirect('/img/street.jpg', { sRGB: true });   // sRGB-encoded photo
```

Any equirectangular (lat-long) image. `sRGB: true` makes the GPU linearize on sample — use it for
ordinary photos and JPEGs, leave it off for true HDR data that is already linear.

Failure is **loud**: a 404 throws rather than silently shipping a black environment.

### 1.3 An indoor / studio look

Same API, different content. A studio HDRI gives you soft box reflections; a small `intensity` with
a bright `zenith` and dark `ground` gives a neutral turntable look:

```ts
env.setProceduralSky({
    zenith: [1, 1, 1], horizon: [0.5, 0.5, 0.5], ground: [0.05, 0.05, 0.05],
    sunDir: [0, -1, 0], sunIntensity: 0,          // no disc — pure ambient dome
});
env.setIntensity(0.6);
```

`sunIntensity: 0` disables the disc entirely, which is the "overcast / lightbox" case.

### 1.3b Analytic daylight, and skies as objects

A sky is a **`SkySource`** — an object you hand to `setSky`, not a method on the system. The source
supplies one WGSL function, `sampleSky(dir)`, which the module injects into **both** the IBL bake
and the skybox fragment. The sky you are lit by and the sky you see are therefore the same function
by construction ([`environment-sky-design.md`](../environment-sky-design.md)).

```ts
import { EnvironmentSystem, PreethamSky } from 'null-graph/environment';

env.setSky(new PreethamSky({
    turbidity: 2.8,               // 1.8 = pristine alpine, 10 = urban haze
    groundAlbedo: [0.15, 0.14, 0.12],
    sunDir: [-0.4, -1.0, -0.35],  // TRAVEL direction, as everywhere in the engine
    sunAngularRadius: 0.266,      // degrees — the TRUE sun
}));

env.sky.setSunDirection(newDir);  // params only, no rebuild — call it per frame if you like
```

Preetham et al. 1999: the sky's luminance gradient, horizon brightening and circumsolar glow are
**derived** from turbidity and a sun direction rather than authored, which is what lets one number
drive a whole day instead of nine colour ramps. About 30 constants and 40 flops.

Its failure mode is documented rather than hidden: the fit **degrades below roughly 5° solar
elevation** and the model can dip negative near the horizon at high turbidity. The shipped path
clamps to non-negative, and sunset fidelity is what the later phases in the series are for.

**Why `sunAngularRadius: 0.266` is newly meaningful.** The real sun is 0.53° across. Until the
skybox evaluated `sampleSky` per pixel it sampled the 128²-per-face prefiltered cube — **0.70° per
texel** — so a physically sized disc was sub-texel and the shipped `sunCos` default drew one 6.8×
too wide on purpose. Per-pixel evaluation is the default now, and the GPU suite measures the disc
back at 0.265°.

**Writing your own source** is the whole extension story — no engine edit, no `if (procedural)`
branch, no new kernel:

```ts
class MySky implements SkySource {
    readonly name = 'MySky';
    readonly paramFloats = 8;
    getShaderLayout(base: number): ShaderSkyLayout { /* WGSL reading skyParams[base + i] */ }
    writeParams(out: Float32Array, base: number): void { /* out-parameter, no allocation */ }
}
```

Hosek–Wilkie is better than Preetham at sunset and is deliberately **not** shipped — it is ~2,700
lines of fitted coefficients, which is data rather than design. Because of this seam, you can add
it yourself without touching the module. See
[`environment-shader-reference.md`](./environment-shader-reference.md) §3.4 for the WGSL contract.

### 1.3c Where the skybox gets its colour

```ts
env.setSkyParams({ cheapSky: 0 });   // DEFAULT — evaluate sampleSky per pixel
env.setSkyParams({ cheapSky: 1, blurMip: 3 });   // sample the prefiltered cube instead
```

| | `cheapSky: 0` (default) | `cheapSky: 1` |
|---|---|---|
| Resolution | per pixel | 0.70°/texel at `prefilterMips: 6` |
| Cost | the source's evaluator, on background pixels only | one cube sample |
| `blurMip` | **ignored** | selects the roughness mip |
| Use it for | anything with detail: a sun disc, a horizon, a sharp imported sky | a deliberately soft backdrop, or a source with no analytic form |

The two agree to the last bit where they overlap — `cheapSky: 1` reproduces the pre-1.1 image
exactly (GPU test T4). **`blurMip` only has meaning in cheap mode**: under the default there is no
mip chain to select, so setting it alone does nothing. If you were using `blurMip` for a soft
background, pass `cheapSky: 1` alongside it.

`EquirectSky` benefits without any flag: its per-pixel path samples the **source** cube at mip 0
(512² by default, 0.176°/texel) instead of the prefiltered 128², a 4× angular improvement from
nothing but reading a different texture. That path needs `keepSourceCube: true`, and says so
loudly if it does not have it.

### 1.4 A complete day/night cycle

```ts
import {
    EnvironmentSystem, NightSky, PreethamSky, SkyComposite, StarField, TimeOfDay,
} from 'null-graph/environment';

const env = new EnvironmentSystem(engine, {
    updateMode: 'amortized',
    keepSourceCube: true,        // required — the prefilter re-reads the source
});

env.setSky(new SkyComposite({
    day: new PreethamSky({ turbidity: 2.8 }),
    night: new NightSky({ latitudeDeg: 45 }),
}));

const stars = new StarField(engine, { latitudeDeg: 45, maxStars: 9100 });

const tod = new TimeOfDay({
    mode: 'artistic',
    timeScale: 60,
    rebakeThresholdDeg: 0.25,
    exposureCoupling: 'off',
});

const skyPass = env.getSkyPass({
    colorAttachments,
    depthStencilAttachment,
    size: [width, height],
    targetFormat: 'rgba16float',
});
stars.attach(env);                    // second additive batch in the same pass
```

Per frame, update the clock before asking the environment for bake stages:

```ts
tod.advance(dt);
tod.applyTo({ environment: env, stars });

const bakeStages = env.getBakeStages();  // shared empty array while clean
engine.render([...bakeStages, ...restBeforeSky, skyPass, ...post.getPassSequence()]);
if (bakeStages.length > 0) env.copySHToParams();
```

`'amortized'` refreshes the source cube, **one prefilter mip**, and SH on each active bake frame.
At the default 6 mips a triggered environment fully refreshes over 6 frames. It does **not** run
unconditionally: `TimeOfDay` invalidates the bake after the sun, or a night-weighted moon, has
accumulated `rebakeThresholdDeg` of angular motion. Daytime lunar motion is suppressed by
`1 - dayFactor`. At the default `0.25°`, solar motion triggers roughly once per minute in real time
and about every four frames at 1000× speed.

Do not call `setProceduralSky` or `setSky` per frame. A source is installed once; `TimeOfDay`
updates it through the optional full `SkySource.setCelestialState` handoff, re-serializes its
parameters, and declares bake dirtiness. See [`time-of-day.md`](./time-of-day.md) for lights,
shadows, exposure, and astronomical mode, and [`night-sky.md`](./night-sky.md) for catalogue and
resize handling.

### 1.5 A rotatable environment

```ts
env.setRotation(performance.now() * 0.0001);
```

Rotates the diffuse SH response and the specular lookup **and the skybox** by the same yaw, so the
three cannot drift apart. Cheap — it is one float in a uniform, not a re-bake.

### 1.6 Worker-computed / precomputed irradiance

The SH set is 27 floats. You can compute it off-thread (or ship it from a previous session) and
hand it over, skipping the projection entirely:

```ts
env.setRawSH(coefficients);    // 9 vec3, envMath order — the setRawData contract
```

`projectSHL2FromCube` in `envMath` is the same math, pure and GPU-free, so a Worker can produce
exactly what the GPU kernel would.

### 1.7 Where Phase 1 stops

Everything above is **one global environment**. If your scene is entirely outdoors, or entirely one
room, that is the correct amount of machinery. The moment you need "dark inside, bright outside,"
you need Phase 2 — which is **shipped**: see [`probes.md`](./probes.md).

| Want | Where |
|---|---|
| Indirect light that **varies through the scene** | ✅ Phase 2 — irradiance volumes ([`probes.md`](./probes.md)) |
| **Local** reflections (a mirror that reflects *this room*) | ✅ Phase 2 — reflection probes |
| Reflections of **scene geometry**, not just the sky | ✅ Phase 2 — probe capture |
| Multi-bounce colour bleeding | ✅ Phase 2 — captures read the previous volume |
| Analytic **atmospheric scattering**, volumetric clouds | ◻ v2.0 ([tree §8](../architecture-tree.md#8-environment)) |
| **Fog**, weather, wind, water, terrain | ◻ planned — the Environment module's other branches |
| Screen-space reflections | Post's job, complementary to IBL |

Phase 2 layers on top: it keeps this system as its **fallback outside the volume** and as the
**ambient its captures shade against**, so nothing here becomes redundant.

## 2. The minimum working setup

```ts
import { EnvironmentSystem } from 'null-graph/environment';
import { LightSystem } from 'null-graph/lights';

const lights = new LightSystem(engine, {
    technique: 'clustered-forward',
    capacity: { point: 32, directional: 1, spot: 8 },
    clusterConfig: { grid: [16, 9, 24], maxLightsPerTile: 32 },
});

const env = new EnvironmentSystem(engine, {
    sourceSize: 512,        // cube face size the bake works from
    prefilterMips: 6,       // roughness levels: mip L = roughness L/(mips-1)
    prefilterSamples: 128,  // GGX importance samples per texel
    intensity: 1.0,
});
env.setProceduralSky({ /* §1.1 */ });

// 1. Bake once. In 'once' mode the stages retire after this frame.
engine.render([...env.getBakeStages()]);
env.copySHToParams();       // moves the projected SH into the uniform (§3.3)

// 2. Build the material with BOTH lighting layouts.
const indirect = env.getShaderLayout();
const batch = vis.createInstanceDrawBatch(scenePass, 'rock', 0, {
    material: { kind: 'pbr', instance: pbr, lighting: lights.getShaderLayout(), indirect },
});

// 3. Bind the COMBINED group 2 — this call, not LightSystem.applyToBatch (§3.2).
env.applyToBatch(batch, lights);

// 4. Every frame.
function frame() {
    engine.updateCamera(camera);
    lights.upload();
    engine.render([
        ...vis.getComputeStages(),
        scenePass,
        env.getSkyPass({ colorAttachments, depthStencilAttachment }),
        ...post.getPassSequence(),
    ]);
    requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}
```

## 3. The three things that are easy to get wrong

### 3.1 Order the sky pass **after** the opaque pass

The skybox draws with `depthCompare: 'less-equal'` and `depthWriteEnabled: false`, at depth
`0.999999`. It fills only where nothing was drawn. Put it **before** the scene and it is
overdrawn — put it after and it is a background, which is what you want and also fewer shaded
pixels.

### 3.2 `env.applyToBatch(batch, lights)` replaces `lights.applyToBatch(batch)`

Core WebGPU guarantees **four** bind groups and NullGraph spends all four (0 engine, 1 material,
2 lights, 3 shadows). Indirect lighting therefore shares **group 2** with the lights — bindings 3–6,
alongside the lights at 0–2.

Because a bind group is built in one call, exactly one owner may build group 2. `EnvironmentSystem`
is that owner when IBL is in play, which is why it takes the `LightSystem` as an argument:

```ts
env.applyToBatch(batch, lights);      // ✅ builds lights 0–2 AND environment 3–6
```

```ts
lights.applyToBatch(batch);           // ❌ overwrites group 2 — the env bindings vanish
env.applyToBatch(batch, lights);      //    (this throws, naming the problem)
```

### 3.3 Call `copySHToParams()` after the bake

The SH projection is a compute shader, so it writes a *storage buffer*. The fragment shader reads
`EnvParams`, a *uniform*. `copySHToParams()` is the GPU-side copy that bridges them — one
144-byte `copyBufferToBuffer`, no readback, no stall.

Skip it and the **specular half works while the diffuse half is black**, which reads as "SH is
broken" rather than "nothing copied it." Call it after `engine.render([...getBakeStages()])` when
that call returned one or more stages. In amortized mode that means each **active bake frame**, not
each clean frame. It is a no-op before the first bake.

## 4. `EnvironmentConfig`

| Field | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `sourceSize` | `512` | Cube face size the bake works from. **Power of two ≥ 8** — the mip chain and the 8×8 SH mip assume it. |
| `prefilterMips` | `6` | Roughness levels in the specular cube. Must not exceed `log2(sourceSize)+1`. Base face is `2^(mips+1)` px, so 6 → 128². |
| `prefilterSamples` | `128` | GGX importance samples per prefiltered texel. Bake-time cost only. |
| `lutSize` | `256` | BRDF LUT resolution. Scene-independent; 256² is plenty. |
| `intensity` | `1.0` | Multiplies both indirect terms. |
| `horizonFade` | `1.0` | Fades specular reflections pointing below the horizon. `0` disables. |
| `updateMode` | `'once'` | `'once'` retires the bake; `'amortized'` refreshes one mip per active invalidation frame and is idle while clean. |
| `keepSourceCube` | `false`* | Retain the source cube after baking. *Defaults `true` when `updateMode: 'amortized'`, which **requires** it. |
| `environmentGroup` | `2` | Must equal the `LightSystem`'s group. Anything else throws (§3.2). |

## 5. API reference

### Sources

| Method | Notes |
|---|---|
| `setSky(source)` | Install a `SkySource`. The mechanism; the two below forward to it. Rebuilds the bake chain. Must precede the first `getSkyPass()`. |
| `setProceduralSky(sky)` | `setSky(new GradientSky(sky))`. Analytic gradient + sun disc, no asset. |
| `setEquirect(url, { sRGB? })` | `async`. Loads a lat-long image, then `setSky(new EquirectSky(...))`. Throws loudly on failure. Needs `keepSourceCube: true`. |
| `setRawSH(coeffs)` | Adopt 27 precomputed SH floats, skipping projection. |
| `sky` | The installed source, typed — `env.sky.setSunDirection(dir)`. Throws before `setSky`. |

**Shipped sources and decorators:**

| Source | Config | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GradientSky` | `ProceduralSkyConfig` | The default. `zenith` / `horizon` / `ground` (linear HDR), `sunDir` (travel direction), `sunIntensity`, optional `sunCos` (default `0.9995` ≈ 1.8° radius). ~20 flops; numerically identical to the pre-1.1 sky. |
| `EquirectSky` | `{ equirect: GPUTextureView }` | Bake reads the 2D asset, skybox reads the source cube at mip 0. Requires `keepSourceCube: true`. |
| `PreethamSky` | `{ turbidity?, groundAlbedo?, sunDir?, sunAngularRadius?, sunDiscIntensity? }` | Analytic daylight (§1.3b). `setSunDirection` / `setTurbidity` rewrite params without a rebuild. |
| `AtmosphereSky` | `(atmosphere, { sunAngularRadius?, sunDiscIntensity? })` | Physical Rayleigh/Mie/ozone daylight backed by `Atmosphere` LUTs. Splice `atmosphere.getStages()` before the environment bake and sky pass. See [`atmosphere.md`](./atmosphere.md). |
| `NightSky` | `NightSkyConfig` | Resolved moon, earthshine, night dome, Milky Way, airglow, and horizon glow. Normally the night child of `SkyComposite`. |
| `SkyComposite` | `{ day, night, dayFactor? }` | Renames and blends two analytic `SkySource`s into one evaluator. `TimeOfDay` drives `dayFactor`. |

`StarField` is not a `SkySource`: it is the separate unresolved point-source draw. See
[`night-sky.md`](./night-sky.md).

### Frame graph

| Method | Notes |
|---|---|
| `getBakeStages()` | The compute stages to splice in. Returns a shared empty array while clean. After an amortized invalidation, emits source + one prefilter mip + SH per call until every mip is refreshed. Throws if no source is set. |
| `invalidateBake()` | Declare that source parameters outside `TimeOfDay` changed. In `'once'` mode, re-arms the full bake; in `'amortized'`, starts one bounded all-mip refresh cycle. Repeated calls during a cycle coalesce. |
| `copySHToParams()` | GPU copy: projected SH → `EnvParams`. Call after the bake (§3.3). |
| `getSkyPass({ colorAttachments, depthStencilAttachment?, size?, targetFormat? })` | The skybox pass. Created once, cached. Splice **after** the opaque pass. |
| `getCreatedSkyPass()` | Return the cached pass for an additive decorator such as `StarField`; throws if it has not been created. |
| `skyTargetFormat` | Colour format frozen into the cached sky-pass pipelines. |

### Material bridge

| Method | Notes |
|---|---|
| `getShaderLayout()` | The `ShaderIndirectLayout` to pass as `indirect`. Throws if no source is set. |
| `applyToBatch(batch, lights)` | Builds the **combined** group-2 bind group. Use instead of `lights.applyToBatch` (§3.2). |

### Runtime knobs

| Method | Notes |
|---|---|
| `setRotation(yawRadians)` | Rotates diffuse, specular, and sky together. |
| `setIntensity(x)` | Scales both indirect terms. |
| `setSkyParams({ exposure?, yaw?, blurMip?, cheapSky? })` | Every field **persists** — a later call that omits one leaves it alone. `yaw` is the environment rotation, so setting it here is equivalent to `setRotation` and keeps the SH, specular and skybox locked. `blurMip` applies only when `cheapSky` is 1 (§1.3c). |

Changes outside `TimeOfDay` must declare their own bake dirtiness. For example, changing
Preetham turbidity updates source-owned CPU state; re-serialize it and invalidate the IBL bake:

```ts
const sky = new PreethamSky({ turbidity: 2.8 });
env.setSky(sky);

sky.setTurbidity(5.0);
env.setSkyParams({});      // upload the source's changed params
env.invalidateBake();     // refresh source cube, prefilter mips, and SH
```

If the same sky is driven by `TimeOfDay`, its `turbidity` config should match the
`PreethamSky` value so the directional-light radiance and visible disc use the same extinction
curve. Runtime turbidity changes need the application to keep those two authored values aligned.

### Introspection

`specularView`, `sourceView`, `brdfView`, `sampler`, `paramsBuffer`, `shStorageBuffer`, `isBaked`,
`bakeInvalidated`, `sky`, `destroy()`.

`bakeInvalidated` is true before the initial bake and while an amortized invalidation still has
prefilter mips outstanding. `TimeOfDay.envDirty` is the celestial trigger for the current update;
the environment flag describes the whole multi-frame refresh cycle.

## 6. Materials that consume it

`indirect` is optional everywhere. Without it, every fragment is **byte-identical** to what it was
before this module existed.

| Material | Uses |
|---|---|
| `pbr` | Diffuse **and** specular — the full split-sum term |
| `lambert` | Diffuse only |
| `toon` | Diffuse only |
| `basic`, `emissive`, `matcap` | Nothing — unlit by definition |

Both the normal batch path and the GPU-culled visibility path accept it:

```ts
// visibility
vis.createInstanceDrawBatch(pass, 'rock', 0, {
    material: { kind: 'pbr', instance: pbr, lighting, indirect },
});

// direct
buildPBRShader({ useSkinning: false, lighting, indirect });
```

**With shadows**, compose all three — shadows decorate the *direct* layout, the environment supplies
the *indirect* one, and they do not interact:

```ts
material: { kind: 'pbr', instance: pbr, lighting: shadows.wrapLighting(lights), indirect }
```

## 7. Cost

| | |
|---|---|
| Bake (`'once'`) | source cube + `log2(size)` mips + `prefilterMips` prefilter dispatches + LUT + SH. One frame, then **zero**. |
| Frame (`'once'`) | Nothing. No dispatch, no upload, no allocation. |
| Active bake frame (`'amortized'`) | One source-cube fill + one prefilter mip + the SH projection. |
| Clean frame (`'amortized'`) | Nothing. `getBakeStages()` returns a shared empty array until `invalidateBake()`. |
| Shading | Two texture samples (prefiltered cube + LUT) and a 9-term SH dot product per pixel. |
| Memory | 512² source cube ≈ 8 MB (releasable) · 128²×6 specular ≈ 200 KB · 256² LUT ≈ 256 KB · `EnvParams` 176 B |

## 8. Errors

Every failure names the offender and the way out.

| Condition | Message |
|---|---|
| Shading before a source is set | `getShaderLayout() called before a source was set; call setEquirect() or setProceduralSky() first.` |
| `sourceSize` not a power of two | `sourceSize <n> must be a power of two ≥ 8; the mip chain and the SH projection mip assume it.` |
| Too many prefilter mips | `prefilterMips <n> exceeds log2(sourceSize)+1 = <m>.` |
| Wrong bind group | `environmentGroup <n> must equal the LightSystem's group (2); core WebGPU guarantees only 4 bind groups and all four are in use.` |
| Group 2 already bound | `batch already has a group-2 bind group from LightSystem.applyToBatch(); use EnvironmentSystem.applyToBatch(batch, lights) to build the combined group instead.` |
| Equirect failed to load | `failed to load equirect "<url>" (...); falling back would silently ship a black environment — set a procedural sky explicitly instead.` |
| Amortized without a retained source | `updateMode "amortized" requires keepSourceCube: true; the prefilter reads the source every refresh.` |

**Sky sources** — all build-time, none in the frame loop:

| Condition | Message |
|---|---|
| A cube-backed source on a system that releases the cube | `EnvironmentSystem: EquirectSky samples the source cube, but keepSourceCube is false — the cube is released after the bake. Construct with { keepSourceCube: true }.` |
| `setSky` after the skybox pipeline was compiled | `EnvironmentSystem: setSky(<name>) must be called before the first getSkyPass(); the compiled skybox pipeline has the previous source layout.` |
| `paramFloats` changed since `setSky` | `SkySource "<name>" declares paramFloats=<n>, but the sky batch was created with strideFloats=<m>. The stride is fixed at batch creation — paramFloats must not change after setSky().` |
| A source whose `wgslLogic` lacks `sampleSky` | `SkySource "<name>" does not define sampleSky(dir: vec3<f32>) -> vec3<f32> (its <site> wgslLogic lacks it).` |
| Generated WGSL contains a backtick | `SkySource "<name>" emitted a backtick, which terminates the template literal carrying it. Use single quotes in WGSL comments.` |
| `getSkyPass` / `env.sky` before a source | `getSkyPass() called before a sky source was set; call setSky() (or setProceduralSky/setEquirect) first.` |
| `StarField.attach(env)` before a sky pass exists | `EnvironmentSystem: no sky pass exists yet; call getSkyPass(target) before attaching a StarField, or pass target to StarField.attach().` |
