16 of 16 384 probes scheduled, getting that wrong means culling for all of them, forever.

### 5.1 Projection to SH-L1

One workgroup of 64 threads strides the probe's 6 × `faceSize²` texels, accumulating 13 floats
(12 coefficients + validity) in workgroup memory, then tree-reduces. WGSL has no `atomic<f32>`, so
this is the same single-workgroup shape Phase 1 uses.

Sky texels (`ndcZ >= 1`) take the prefiltered environment instead of the captured colour — that is
how a probe that sees open sky gets the right answer without the sky being geometry.

Validity comes out of the same pass: a texel whose linear depth is under `spacing × 0.25` counts as
enclosed; past 60 % enclosed the probe is written invalid.

---

## 6. Conventions a CPU mirror must match

`probeMath.ts` mirrors `probeShaders.ts` so the math is testable headless. It is **a second
implementation**, and it drifts. Two traps, both of which have actually bitten:

### 6.1 `cubeTexelSolidAngle` takes different units on each side

| | Signature | Pass |
|---|---|---|
| **WGSL** | `cubeTexelSolidAngle(uv: vec2<f32>, size: u32)` | normalized texel-centre UV |
| **CPU** | `cubeTexelSolidAngle(x, y, size)` | **integer texel indices** |

Same math, different parameterisation, and **no type error** — `number` accepts `0.0625` as happily
as `0`. Passing UVs to the CPU form shrinks every texel's solid angle: Σ comes to 7.78 instead of
4π and the whole projection scales down ~1.6×, silently, with plausible-looking output.

The invariant that catches it: **a constant radiance `c` must project to L0 == `c`**, because the
solid angles sum to exactly 4π. That is U3, and it is worth more than reading the two side by side.

### 6.2 "No depth supplied" is not "everything is sky"

`ndcZ >= 1` is the sky sentinel. The CPU mirror's `depth` argument is optional (the GPU always has
one), and defaulting the absent case to `1` means every texel takes the sky path and the captured
colour is never read — the projection returns zeros. The guard is on *whether depth exists*, not on
its value:

```ts
const hasDepth = opts.depth !== undefined;
const ndcZ = hasDepth ? opts.depth![t] : 0;
if (hasDepth && ndcZ >= 1) { /* sky */ } else { /* colour */ }
```

### 6.3 Fix the mirror toward the kernel — after checking which is right

Both bugs above were in the **CPU** mirror; the WGSL was correct. Fixing them the other way round
would have broken the GPU path to make a test pass. Establish which side is right *first*.

---

## 7. Generated modules

| Builder | Produces |
|---|---|
| `buildProbeStructsWGSL(group)` | bindings 7–13 + `ProbeParams`/`ReflProbe` structs + helpers |
| `buildProbeIndirectLogicWGSL()` | `getIndirectDiffuse` / `getIndirectSpecular`, volume-backed |
| `buildProbeIndirectLayout(envLayout, group)` | the composed `ShaderIndirectLayout` handed to materials |
| `buildProbeProjectionWGSL({ faceSize })` | the capture → SH-L1 projection kernel |
| `buildReflAssembleWGSL()` | capture band → reflection cube face assembly |
| `buildPrefilterWGSL({ …, baseArrayLayer })` | **Phase 1's kernel**, targeting one cube of the array |

That last row is the point: reflection prefiltering is Phase 1's GGX kernel with a layer offset, not
a second implementation.

Every module is parsed with `wgsl_reflect` in the test suite, and the same **no-backtick** rule
applies as Phase 1 — a backtick in a WGSL comment terminates the JS template literal carrying it.

---

## 8. Test map

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| U1 | grid ↔ world round-trip; index/coord round-trip; outside maps outside |
| U2 | trilinear mirror: eight ⅛s between probes, one 1 on a centre (texel-centre alignment) |
| U3 | constant environment → L0 == c (**catches the solid-angle unit mismatch**) |
| U4 | L1 ringing clamped ≥ 0 everywhere |
| U5 | validity 0 ⇒ the lookup equals the global environment *exactly*, not black |
| U6 | parallax reprojects from the capture point, not the box centre |
| U7 | probe weights never exceed 1; the environment gets the remainder |
| U8 | scheduler fairness: no starvation, near ≥ 4× far |
| U9 | the contract is byte-identical to Phase 1's; the material fragment is unchanged |
| U10 | bindings 7–13 exactly once; the diffuse anti-prune holds |
| §11 | config validation messages |

`npm run test:environment` runs Phase 1 and Phase 2 (23 checks). GPU integration is
[`lighting-probes-design.md`](../lighting-probes-design.md) §10 T1–T7.

docs.title: Profiler API Usage
Shadows API Usage
docs.text:
# Shadows API Usage

The `null-graph/shadows` module is the shadow runtime. **Phase 1** is the cascaded shadow map:
one directional light (a sun that occludes), N cascades fitted to the view, depth-only caster
passes, GPU caster culling, and a filtered receiver-side lookup that drops into every existing
material without touching `LightSystem` or the material builders. **Phase 2** turns that into a
*system*: every light type casts, shadow memory is one fixed atlas the engine partitions by
importance, tiles that did not change are not re-rendered, and casters hidden behind other casters
are culled on the GPU.

The load-bearing idea (design §1): **a shadow map is the same draw the main pass already makes,
from a different matrix.** A cascade *is* a `Camera` — an orthographic one — so caster culling is
the existing [`VisibilitySystem`](./visibility.md) cull chain pointed at a different camera
uniform, and the depth pass is the engine's batch primitive with `depthOnly`. Phase 2 generalizes
that `Camera` into a `ShadowView` — a `Camera` plus an atlas rectangle — so a cascade, a spot
cone, and one of six cube faces differ only in how their matrix is built and how big a tile they
get.

- **Phase 1 architecture:** [`shadows-design.md`](../shadows-design.md)
- **Phase 2 architecture (atlas, punctual lights, caching):** [`shadows-atlas-design.md`](../shadows-atlas-design.md)
- **Buffer layouts, WGSL contracts, the material bridge:** [`shadows-shader-reference.md`](./shadows-shader-reference.md)

```ts
import { ShadowSystem } from 'null-graph/shadows';
import { VisibilitySystem, InstanceBuffer } from 'null-graph/visibility';
import { MegabufferBuilder, StandardLayout } from 'null-graph/geometry';
import { LightSystem } from 'null-graph/lights';
```

---

## Do you need this?

| Scene | Use |
|---|---|
| Open world, one dominant sun | **Phase 1** (below) or **Phase 2** with one directional light. |
| Indoor / many local lights | **Phase 2** — spot and point shadows live in the atlas. |
| A mix: a sun plus torches/lamps | **Phase 2** — one atlas, every light type casts. |
| A small diorama, one light | Maybe. A single cascade (`cascades: 1`) is the cheap path. |

Phase 1 is deliberately **one light, N cascades**. Phase 2 is the *system*: many lights, one
atlas, tile caching, occlusion-culled casters. Phase 2 is **additive** — a Phase 1 config (no
`atlasSize`) runs the Phase 1 path unchanged; setting `atlasSize` switches to the atlas.

## What you wire up

```
VisibilitySystem  ──►  the casters (its instances are what occlude)
ShadowSystem      ──►  fits cascades, renders depth, decorates the lighting
LightSystem       ──►  the directional light the shadow matches
materials         ──►  unchanged — they consume incident.attenuation, which the shadow folds into
```

---

## 1. Build geometry + visibility (the casters)

Shadows reuse the visibility instance buffer as the caster set, so build that first (see
[`visibility.md`](./visibility.md)):

```ts
const mega = new MegabufferBuilder(8);
mega.addMesh('rock', rockVerts, rockIndices);
mega.addMesh('ground', groundVerts, groundIndices);

const vis = new VisibilitySystem(engine, { maxInstances: 100_000 });
vis.setGeometry(mega);
```

## 2. Create the shadow system

```ts
const shadows = new ShadowSystem(engine, {
    cascades: 4,
    resolution: 2048,
    shadowDistance: 200,        // NOT camera.far — shadows stop here
    lambda: 0.6,                // split blend: 0 = uniform, 1 = logarithmic
    casterExtrusion: 200,       // how far behind the cascade the near plane reaches
    constantBias: 0.0015,
    normalOffsetTexels: 1.5,
    pcfRadius: 1,               // 1 → 3×3 taps of hardware PCF
    blendTexels: 4.0,           // cascade cross-fade band
    lodBias: 1,                 // casters render one LOD coarser
    visibility: vis,            // required — Phase 1 has no CPU caster path
    shadowGroupIndex: 3,        // bind group for the shadow resources
});
```

| Option | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cascades` | `4` | 1–4. `MAX_CASCADES` sizes the `ShadowData` uniform. |
| `resolution` | `2048` | Power of two — texel snapping assumes it. |
| `shadowDistance` | `200` | Bounds the cascade set. Beyond it, lighting is unshadowed. |
| `lambda` | `0.6` | Practical-split blend (§5.1). |
| `casterExtrusion` | `shadowDistance` | §5.4. Supply the scene's extent along the light if you know it. |
| `constantBias` | `0.0015` | NDC-z bias on the caster (§7.1). |
| `normalOffsetTexels` | `1.5` | Caster normal offset in texels (§7.2). §11 throws if it swamps a cascade. |
| `pcfRadius` | `1` | 0 → hardware 2×2 only, 1 → 3×3, 2 → 5×5. |
| `blendTexels` | `4.0` | Cascade cross-fade band, in split-distance units. |
| `lodBias` | `1` | Coarsens caster LOD selection (§5.5). |
| `visibility` | — | **Required.** The `VisibilitySystem` whose instances are the casters. |
| `shadowGroupIndex` | `3` | Must be ≥ 3 (group 2 is `LightSystem`'s). |
| `allowColorFallback` | `false` | §6.3 escape hatch if `depthOnly` is unavailable. ~1.5–2× pass cost. |

## 3. Register casters

One call per caster mesh. Internally this is `cascades` depth-only indirect batches — one per
cascade layer — each pointed at its cascade's camera with Hi-Z off:

```ts
shadows.registerCaster('rock', rockMeshIndex);
shadows.registerCaster('ground', groundMeshIndex);
```

Draw-call count is `cascades × casterMeshes`, **independent of instance count** — the same
property the main pass has. 4 cascades × 6 caster meshes with 200 000 instances is 24 draws.

## 4. Decorate the lighting + bind the receiver

`wrapLighting` returns a layout of the same shape as `LightSystem.getShaderLayout()`, whose
`getIncidentLight` calls the original and folds the shadow term into `attenuation`. Lambert, Toon,
and PBR all consume `incident.attenuation`, so all three gain shadows with zero edits:

```ts
const lights = new LightSystem(engine, { technique: 'standard', capacity: { directional: 1, point: 0, spot: 0 } });
const shadowedLighting = shadows.wrapLighting(lights);

const batch = vis.createInstanceDrawBatch(scenePass, 'rock', rockMeshIndex, {
    vertexLayouts: StandardLayout.getWebGPUDescriptor(),
    material: { kind: 'pbr', instance: rockMat, lighting: shadowedLighting },
});
lights.applyToBatch(batch, 2);        // the light buffers at group 2
shadows.applyToBatch(batch);          // shadowMaps + sampler + ShadowData at group 3
```

Phase 1 shadows **exactly one directional light**, identified by direction match (two directional
lights pointing the same way *are* the same light). Set the sun direction on both systems:

```ts
shadows.setLight([-0.5, -1.0, -0.3]);   // travel direction; normalized internally
// …and the matching directional light's dir_rad in the LightSystem data.
```

## 5. Render

`update(camera)` fits the cascades and writes the buffers; then splice the caster culls and the
depth passes ahead of the scene pass:

```ts
function frame() {
    vis.setInstances(instances.data, instances.count);

    shadows.setLight(sunDir);
    shadows.update(camera);             // splits, sphere fit, snap, write N cascade buffers + ShadowData
    vis.upload();

    engine.render([
        ...vis.getComputeStages(),      // main-view culls AND the per-cascade caster culls
        ...shadows.getComputeStages(),  // empty by design — caster culls ride vis's chain
        ...shadows.getPasses(),         // N depth-only passes, one per cascade layer
        scenePass,                      // materials sample the cascade array
        ...post.getPassSequence(),
    ]);
}
```

`update()` writes `cascades × 432 + cascades × 16 + 352` bytes from persistent typed arrays — no
allocation. It takes only matrices and scalars, so a worker can compute the cascade array and hand
it over with `shadows.setRawCascades(viewF32, shadowDataF32)` (the `LightSystem.setRawData`
contract).

---

# Phase 2 — the atlas, punctual lights, and caching

Set `atlasSize` and the system switches from the per-cascade array to **one atlas texture** that
every light type shares. The unifying move (atlas-design §1): a `ShadowView` — a `Camera` plus a
render target — becomes a `ShadowView` **plus an atlas rectangle**. A cascade, a spot cone, and
one of six cube faces differ only in how their matrix is built and how big a tile they get.

## P2.1 Create the atlas system

```ts
const shadows = new ShadowSystem(engine, {
    atlasSize: 4096,            // the ONE fixed allocation — every light shares it
    maxTileSize: 2048,          // largest tile a single view may request
    maxViews: 64,               // cascades + spots + 6×points
    maxSlots: 64,               // shadow-casting lights
    cascades: 4,                // for any directional light
    shadowDistance: 200,
    constantBias: 0.0015,
    pcfRadius: 1,
    updateMode: 'round-robin',  // 'every-frame' | 'on-demand' | 'round-robin'
    refreshPerFrame: 2,         // clean views refreshed per frame in round-robin
    lightViewOcclusion: true,   // Hi-Z on the light view (atlas-design §7.2)
    visibility: vis,
    shadowGroupIndex: 3,
});
```

| Phase 2 option | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `atlasSize` | — | **Setting it selects the atlas path.** Power of two. 4096² ≈ 32 MB. |
| `maxTileSize` | `2048` | Top of the tile ladder (`2048, 1024, 512, 256, 128`). |
| `maxViews` | `64` | Hard cap on views. Exceeding it throws the §11 error naming the light. |
| `maxSlots` | `64` | Hard cap on shadow-casting lights. |
| `updateMode` | `'every-frame'` | §8.1. `'every-frame'` is always correct; `'on-demand'` renders only dirty views; `'round-robin'` also refreshes `refreshPerFrame` clean views/frame. |
| `refreshPerFrame` | `2` | Bounds the damage from a missed `invalidate()` to a few frames. |
| `cubeFovMarginTexels` | `pcfRadius` | The cube-face fov margin. §11 throws when it's smaller than `pcfRadius` (face seams). |
| `lightViewOcclusion` | `false` | §7.2 — Hi-Z occlusion-cull casters on the light view, reusing `HiZPyramid` over last frame's atlas. |

## P2.2 Register lights

`registerLight` returns the **shadow slot**; write `slot + 1` into the light record's
`spot_params.z` (float 14 of the 16-float record) so the receiver can find the light's views. `0`
in that field means "does not cast" (atlas-design §4.3):

```ts
const sunSlot  = shadows.registerLight({ kind: 'directional', name: 'sun' });
const lampSlot = shadows.registerLight({ kind: 'point', name: 'lamp', position: [2, 3, 1], range: 30 });
const spotSlot = shadows.registerLight({ kind: 'spot',  name: 'spot', position: [0, 5, 0],
                                         direction: [0, -1, 0], range: 20, outerCos: Math.cos(0.6) });

lightData[sunLightIndex  * 16 + 14] = sunSlot + 1;   // spot_params.z
lightData[lampLightIndex * 16 + 14] = lampSlot + 1;
lightData[spotLightIndex * 16 + 14] = spotSlot + 1;
```

A directional light owns `cascades` consecutive views, a spot one, a point exactly six in
`+X,−X,+Y,−Y,+Z,−Z` order (so face selection is arithmetic). The Phase 1 direction match is
**deleted** in the atlas path — the slot is explicit, so two identical directional lights no
longer collide.

## P2.3 Register casters + render

Same calls as Phase 1; the atlas path puts every view's draws into **one** pass:

```ts
shadows.registerCaster('rock', rockMeshIndex);

function frame() {
    vis.setInstances(instances.data, instances.count);
    shadows.setLight(sunDir);           // the directional light's travel direction
    shadows.update(camera);             // builds every view, allocates/evicts tiles, writes tables
    vis.upload();

    engine.render([
        ...vis.getComputeStages(),      // main-view culls AND the per-view caster culls
        ...shadows.getComputeStages(),  // the light-view Hi-Z build, when lightViewOcclusion is on
        shadows.getAtlasPass(),         // ONE depth-only pass, one viewport-scoped batch per (view × mesh)
        scenePass,
        ...post.getPassSequence(),
    ]);
}
```

Draw-call count is `views × casterMeshes` in one pass, independent of instance count — and the
caching below removes the views whose tiles did not change.

## P2.4 Caching — not re-rendering what did not change

NullGraph has no scene graph, so it cannot know a caster moved — **dirtiness is declared, not
inferred** (atlas-design §8.1). The default `updateMode: 'every-frame'` re-renders everything
(always correct). To cache:

```ts
const shadows = new ShadowSystem(engine, { atlasSize: 4096, updateMode: 'on-demand', /* … */ });

// When a caster that light `lampSlot` sees moves:
shadows.invalidate(lampSlot);         // that light's views re-render this frame
```

A view is re-rendered when its matrix changed (the light moved), its tile was resized/evicted/
newly allocated, the caller called `invalidate(slot)`, or `updateMode` is `'every-frame'`.
`'round-robin'` additionally refreshes `refreshPerFrame` clean views per frame — the pragmatic
setting for a world where some casters are "mostly static."

## P2.5 Eviction and the budget

The atlas is allocated once; when demand exceeds it, the system **evicts the least-important
resident views** (never cascades — the sun is not allowed to lose its shadow because forty torches
got close to the camera). An evicted view's light samples as **fully lit** — never black — and the
eviction is reported through `shadows.shadowAtlas.report()`, never silent. Exceeding `maxViews`
is a hard error naming the light.

---

## Errors (fail-loud, at build/compile time)

| Condition | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `cascades` outside 1–4 | throws — `MAX_CASCADES` sizes the `ShadowData` uniform |
| `resolution` not a power of two | throws — texel snapping assumes it |
| `shadowGroupIndex` ≤ 2 | throws — collides with `LightSystem`'s `@group(2)` |
| `registerCaster` without `visibility` | throws — Phase 1 has no CPU caster path |
| `getPasses()` before `update(camera)` | throws — cascade matrices unset |
| `wrapLighting` on a technique with no layout | throws — needs `standard` or `clustered-forward` |
| `getIncidentLight` marker moved in `LightSystem` | throws — the decorator is out of date |
| normal offset > 2% of a cascade's extent | throws — contact shadows would detach |
| **Phase 2:** more views than `maxViews` | throws — names the light; raise `maxViews` or stop shadowing it |
| **Phase 2:** a single view larger than the atlas | throws — raise `atlasSize` or lower `maxTileSize` |
| **Phase 2:** atlas full but fragmented | throws — `freePx`² free across `k` regions; lower `maxTileSize` or raise `atlasSize` |
| **Phase 2:** shadow slot > 254 | throws — `spot_params.z` encodes `slot+1` as a float |
| **Phase 2:** `cubeFovMarginTexels` < `pcfRadius` | throws — face seams will appear |
| **Phase 2:** `invalidate(n)` on an unregistered slot | throws — `registerLight()` returns the valid range |
| **Phase 2:** `registerLight` without `atlasSize` | throws — punctual lights need the atlas path |

## Notes & limits

- **Phase 1: one directional light.** Spot/point shadows need the Phase 2 atlas (`atlasSize`).
- **Phase 1: no Hi-Z on the light view.** Caster culling is frustum-only (Phase 2 adds occlusion
  via `lightViewOcclusion`).
- **Fixed-radius PCF only.** PCSS / VSM / ESM / MSM are out of scope for both phases (the atlas
  makes them *possible*; picking one is a separate quality decision).
- **All bias lives on the caster.** `PipelineConfig` exposes no `depthBias`/`cullMode`, and the
  receiver has no normal in scope (§8.2) — so the constant and normal offsets are applied in the
  depth-only vertex shader. This is why Phase 1 needs no rasterizer-state change.
- **Conservative always beats clever.** A caster wrongly culled is a missing shadow in the *lit*
  image. Every cascade fit errs toward including geometry (§5.3 sphere fit, §5.4 extrusion), and
  the atlas-wide Hi-Z is a *max* reduction, so neighbour bleed causes under-culling, never
  over-culling (atlas-design §7.2).
- **The atlas needs per-batch viewport support** (atlas-design §12.1) — `PipelineConfig.viewport`,
  six lines in `RenderPipeline`, inert for every existing batch. The zero-change alternative (a
  clip-space tile remap) **bleeds** into neighbouring tiles and is not the baseline (§6.2).
- **Testing.** The cascade math, the atlas allocator, the view builders, the cube face select, the
  tap clamp, the slot packing, and every generated WGSL module are covered headless by
  `npm run test:shadows`. The GPU integration scenes live in `test/shadows-gpu/` (T1–T8 — shadow
  presence, caster culling, depth range, no shimmer/crawl, cascade seams, beyond-distance, the
  viewport contract) and run on a real device with `npm run test:gpu` (Node + Dawn) or
  `npm run test:gpu:browser` (headless Chrome). The atlas-design §10 scenes are not written yet.

docs.title: Shadows — Shader & Buffer Reference
docs.text:
# Shadows — Shader & Buffer Reference

Companion to [`shadows.md`](./shadows.md) (usage),
[`shadows-design.md`](../shadows-design.md) (Phase 1 architecture), and
[`shadows-atlas-design.md`](../shadows-atlas-design.md) (Phase 2 architecture). This is the
**contract layer**: exact byte layouts, WGSL bindings, the generated kernels, and how the shadow
term reaches a material.

Read this when you are writing a custom receiver shader, debugging a bind-group error, computing
cascades in a worker, or wiring shadows into a hand-written material.

> **Phase 1 vs Phase 2.** Phase 1 (no `atlasSize`) uses a `depth24plus` **2D array**, one layer
> per cascade, and the `ShadowData` uniform — §1–§5 below. Phase 2 (`atlasSize` set) uses **one
> atlas texture** plus runtime `shadowViews`/`shadowSlots` storage tables — §A1–§A5. The caster
> vertex shader (§5) and the engine touchpoints (§7) are shared.

---

## 1. Buffer layouts

Every structure is 16-byte aligned and worker-fillable. Sizes are exact.

### 1.1 The cascade camera — 432 bytes (108 floats)

One `GPUBuffer` per cascade, filled with the **exact** `Camera` layout (`core/Camera.ts:35`) so
`CAMERA_STRUCT_WGSL` reads it unchanged. That is the whole trick: a cascade is indistinguishable
from a camera to every existing shader.

| Floats | Bytes | Field | Cascade value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–15 | 0–63 | `viewProj` | `orthoZO(l,r,b,t,0,2r+e) × lookAt(eye, center, up)` |
| 16–31 | 64–127 | `view` | the light's `lookAt` |
| 32–47 | 128–191 | `proj` | the `orthoZO` |
| 48–63 | 192–255 | `invViewProj` | inverse (unused by the cull path; filled for completeness) |
| 64–79 | 256–319 | `invView` | inverse |
| 80–95 | 320–383 | `invProj` | inverse |
| 96–98 | 384–395 | `eyePos` | ortho origin: `center − dir × (radius + extrusion)` |
| 99 | 396 | `simTime` | copied from the main camera |
| 100 | 400 | `zNear` | `0` (the extruded near plane, §5.4) |
| 101 | 404 | `zFar` | `2 × radius + extrusion` |
| 102 | 408 | `fovRads` | the **virtual** fov reproducing this cascade's texel density (§5.5) |
| 103 | 412 | `aspect` | `1.0` (cascades are square) |

`buildCascades()` / `fitCascade()` produce this array; `update()` writes it verbatim into the
cascade's buffer. A worker can fill the same 108 floats and hand them over via
`setRawCascades(views, shadowData)` — `views` is `cascades` packed 108-float blocks.

> **ZO, not NO.** The projection is `mat4.orthoZO` — WebGPU clip is `z ∈ [0,1]`. Swapping in the
> NO form (`ortho`) silently moves the near plane, the same trap `Camera.ts:62-66` documents for
> perspective. Pinned by test U4.

### 1.2 `ShadowCasterParams` — 16 bytes (uniform, per cascade)

One per cascade, written by `update()`. The caster's bias constants are **exact for the cascade
being rendered** — a single shared `ShadowData` cannot serve the caster, because the cascade index
is a per-*pass* property and a uniform-array index would be a per-*vertex* one.

| Float | Field | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `texelWorld` | `2 × radius / resolution` for THIS cascade |
| 1 | `normalOffsetTexels` | `config.normalOffsetTexels` (default 1.5) |
| 2 | `constantBias` | `config.constantBias` (default 0.0015) |
| 3 | `_pad` | 0 |

### 1.3 `ShadowData` — 352 bytes (uniform, one per system)

The receiver uniform, bound at the shadow group (default 3). `MAX_CASCADES = 4` sizes the fixed
array. Written once per frame from a persistent `Float32Array` by `packShadowData()`.

```wgsl
struct ShadowCascade {
    viewProj   : mat4x4<f32>,   // 64 B  world → cascade clip
    splitFar   : f32,           //       view-space depth this cascade covers up to
    texelWorld : f32,           //       world size of one shadow texel (bias + filter radius)
    _pad0      : f32,
    _pad1      : f32,           // 16 B
};                              // 80 B, 16-aligned

struct ShadowData {
    cascades      : array<ShadowCascade, MAX_CASCADES>,   // 80 × 4 = 320 B
    lightDir      : vec4<f32>,   // .xyz normalized light travel direction, .w unused
    cascadeCount  : u32,
    pcfRadius     : u32,         // taps per side: 1 → 3×3, 2 → 5×5, 0 → hardware 2×2 only
    blendTexels   : f32,         // cascade cross-fade band, in split-distance units
    constantBias  : f32,
};                              // 320 + 32 = 352 B
```

`cascadeCount` and `pcfRadius` occupy float slots but hold **raw u32 bits** — `packShadowData`
writes them through a `Uint32Array` view over the same memory (the `InstanceBuffer` contract).

### 1.4 The cascade array (texture)

| Resource | Format / usage | Size |
|---|---|---|
| cascade array | `depth24plus`, `RENDER_ATTACHMENT \| TEXTURE_BINDING`, `depthOrArrayLayers = cascades` | `resolution² × N` |
| per-layer views | `createView({ dimension:'2d', baseArrayLayer:i, arrayLayerCount:1 })` | the render targets |
| sampling view | `createView({ dimension:'2d-array' })` | bound as `texture_depth_2d_array` |
| comparison sampler | `createSampler({ compare:'less', magFilter:'linear', minFilter:'linear' })` | hardware 2×2 PCF |

4 × 2048² `depth24plus` ≈ **16 MB**, allocated once. `depth24plus` is samplable +
comparison-filterable (core WebGPU — no optional feature anywhere), but it is **not**
buffer-copyable, so the GPU tests read it back through a compute pass (`textureLoad` into an f32
storage buffer) — legal in a test, forbidden in the frame loop.

---

## 2. Bind-group contracts

`layout: 'auto'` prunes any binding the shader does not *use*, and supplying an entry for a pruned
binding throws. The generated modules therefore reference exactly what they bind.

### 2.1 The caster pass (depth-only)

Group 0 is engine-fixed by `createBatch`; the caster params ride the shadow group:

| Group | Binding | Resource |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | `camera` — the **cascade's** 432-byte Camera (`PipelineConfig.cameraBuffer`) |
| 0 | 1 | `instances` — the compacted survivors (`batch.storageBuffer`) |
| 3 | 3 | `casterParams` — the per-cascade `ShadowCasterParams` uniform |

The vertex stage genuinely reads both group-0 bindings (the culled instances and the cascade
camera), so nothing is pruned. The caster shader is vertex-only unless `allowColorFallback` adds
the throwaway `fs_main` (§6.3).

### 2.2 The receiver (scene material)

The decorator emits the shadow resources into the **same module** as the light bindings, at the
shadow group (default 3):

| Group | Binding | Resource |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | `camera` (the main view) |
| 1 | — | the material |
| 2 | — | `LightSystem`'s light buffers (hardcoded) |
| 3 | 0 | `shadowMaps : texture_depth_2d_array` |
| 3 | 1 | `shadowSampler : sampler_comparison` |
| 3 | 2 | `shadow : ShadowData` (uniform) |

> **Group 3 by default.** Group 0 is engine-fixed, group 1 is the material on the instance tier,
> group 2 is hardcoded into `LightSystem`'s WGSL. `shadowGroupIndex` is configurable for the
> meshlet tier, where group 1 already holds geometry — but it must be **≥ 3** (the constructor
> throws otherwise).

---

## 3. The decorator — how the shadow term reaches a material

`wrapLighting(lightSystem)` returns a `{ wgslStructs, wgslLogic }` of the same shape as
`LightSystem.getShaderLayout()`. It performs **one deterministic textual rename**, guarded by a
loud error if the marker ever moves:

```ts
const marker = 'fn getIncidentLight(';
wgslLogic.replace(marker, 'fn getIncidentLightUnshadowed(')   // the original, renamed
    + SHADOW_SAMPLING_WGSL                                    // sampleCascade / sampleShadow
    + SHADOW_BIASED_WGSL                                      // shadowFactorBiased (optional)
    + buildShadowDecoratorWGSL(accessor);                     // the new getIncidentLight
```

The replacement `getIncidentLight` calls the original and folds the shadow term into
`attenuation`, reading the light record directly to decide whether *that* light casts:

```wgsl
fn getIncidentLight(i: u32, worldPos: vec3<f32>) -> IncidentLight {
    var inc = getIncidentLightUnshadowed(i, worldPos);
    let rec = ${accessor};                  // standard:  lights[i]
                                            // clustered: globalLights[lightIndices[getClusterData(worldPos).start_offset + i]]
    if (rec.pos_type.w == 2.0 && dot(normalize(rec.dir_rad.xyz), shadow.lightDir.xyz) > 0.999) {
        inc.attenuation = inc.attenuation * sampleShadow(worldPos);
    }
    return inc;
}
```

Lambert, Toon, and PBR all consume `incident.attenuation`, so all three gain shadows with zero
edits. The `accessor` exists (rather than a direction-only test) because Phase 2 replaces the dot
product with an explicit per-light shadow slot carried in the light record's free `spot_params.z`.

> **The guard is the safety story.** U6 pins the rename against the real `LightSystem` output for
> both `standard` and `clustered-forward`, so a rename in `LightSystem.ts` fails a headless test
> rather than silently shipping unshadowed lighting.

### 3.1 Why the receiver has no normal

The material contract is `getIncidentLight(i, worldPos)` — no normal. Recovering the geometric
normal with `dpdx/dpdy(worldPos)` is illegal here: the call sits inside `for (i < lightCount)`
where `lightCount` comes from a cluster lookup and is **non-uniform across the quad**, which
WGSL's `derivative_uniformity` diagnostic rejects. That is the constraint that pushed all bias
onto the caster (§7). A hand-written fragment that *has* `N` in scope may call
`shadowFactorBiased(worldPos, N, L)` for receiver-side normal offset and drop `normalOffsetTexels`
to 0.

---

## 4. The sampling functions

```wgsl
fn sampleShadow(worldPos: vec3<f32>) -> f32 {
    let viewDepth = -(camera.view * vec4<f32>(worldPos, 1.0)).z;
    var c = shadow.cascadeCount;                       // sentinel: beyond the last split
    for (var k = 0u; k < shadow.cascadeCount; k = k + 1u) {
        if (viewDepth < shadow.cascades[k].splitFar) { c = k; break; }
    }
    if (c >= shadow.cascadeCount) { return 1.0; }      // past shadowDistance → fully lit
    let lit = sampleCascade(c, worldPos);
    // Cross-fade into the next cascade over the last blendTexels of this one.
    let edge = shadow.cascades[c].splitFar - shadow.blendTexels;
    if (c + 1u < shadow.cascadeCount && viewDepth > edge) {
        let t = (viewDepth - edge) / shadow.blendTexels;
        return mix(lit, sampleCascade(c + 1u, worldPos), clamp(t, 0.0, 1.0));
    }
    return lit;
}
```

`sampleCascade` projects into the cascade's clip space, flips Y (clip +Y up → texture +V down),
and PCF-filters:

```wgsl
let ref   = ndc.z - shadow.constantBias;
let r     = i32(shadow.pcfRadius);
if (r == 0) { return textureSampleCompareLevel(shadowMaps, shadowSampler, uv, k, ref); }
// else a (2r+1)² grid of hardware-2×2 taps
```

> **`textureSampleCompareLevel`, never the bare `textureSampleCompare`.** The latter takes implicit
> derivatives and is only valid in uniform control flow; every call above sits inside a cascade
> branch and a PCF loop. Using the bare form is a shader-compile error at best and a
> derivative-uniformity trap at worst — pinned by test U7, which asserts the generated WGSL never
> emits `textureSampleCompare(`.

Each tap is hardware 2×2-comparison-filtered by the comparison sampler, so `pcfRadius: 1` is a 3×3
grid of bilinear-PCF taps ≈ a 6×6 kernel.

---

## 5. The caster vertex shader — all bias lives here

`PipelineConfig` exposes neither `depthBias` nor `cullMode`, and the receiver has no normal in
scope (§3.1), so both bias terms live in the depth-only vertex shader, where the normal *is* in
scope and control flow *is* uniform:

```wgsl
@vertex
fn vs_main(@location(0) pos: vec3<f32>, @location(1) normal: vec3<f32>,
           @builtin(instance_index) ii: u32) -> @builtin(position) vec4<f32> {
    let inst = instances[ii];
    let n = normalize(normalMatrixFromModel(inst.model) * normal);
    let world = (inst.model * vec4<f32>(pos, 1.0)).xyz;

    // §7.2 — normal offset, scaled by THIS cascade's world texel size (resolution-correct).
    let biasedWorld = world + n * (casterParams.texelWorld * casterParams.normalOffsetTexels);

    var clipPos = camera.viewProj * vec4<f32>(biasedWorld, 1.0);
    // §7.1 — constant bias in clip space, × w so it is a plain NDC-z offset under ortho (w == 1).
    clipPos.z = clipPos.z + casterParams.constantBias * clipPos.w;
    return clipPos;
}
```

The tradeoff (§7.3): caster-side offset trades **acne** for **peter-panning** — contact shadows
detach by roughly `texelWorld × normalOffsetTexels`. At 2048 over a 40-unit cascade that is ~3 cm
(invisible); at 512 over 200 units it is ~1.2 m (obvious). The first cascade's world extent is what
sets contact-shadow quality — the real argument for cascades over one big map. `update()` throws
(§11) when the computed offset exceeds 2% of a cascade's extent.

---

## 6. Generated kernels

Every generator is exported, so you can print one and read it — the fastest way to debug a
bind-group mismatch.

| Function | Emits |
|---|---|
| `buildShadowCasterWGSL({ shadowGroupIndex, colorFallback })` | the depth-only caster VS (+ optional throwaway FS) |
| `buildShadowBindingsWGSL(group)` | the `@group(g)` shadow resource declarations |
| `buildShadowDecoratorWGSL(accessor)` | the shadowed `getIncidentLight` |

Reusable chunks: `SHADOW_STRUCTS_WGSL`, `SHADOW_SAMPLING_WGSL`, `SHADOW_BIASED_WGSL`. The caster
also reuses `CAMERA_STRUCT_WGSL`, `INSTANCE_STRUCT_WGSL`, and `CULL_CORE_WGSL` from
[`visibilityShaders`](./visibility-shader-reference.md#5-generated-kernels) unchanged — a cascade
is a camera, so `frustumPlanes(camera.viewProj)` and `worldSphereFromModel` work with no
shadow-specific branch.

```ts
import { buildShadowCasterWGSL } from 'null-graph/shadows';
console.log(buildShadowCasterWGSL({}));
```

---

## 7. The engine touchpoints (§12.1)

Phase 1 is the first NullGraph module that asks for a core change. Both are additive, opt-in, and
inert for every existing caller:

```ts
// PipelineConfig.depthOnly — omit the fragment stage and color targets entirely.
// A fragment-less render pipeline is core WebGPU.
engine.createBatch(pass, { /* … */, depthOnly: true });

// PipelineConfig.cameraBuffer — the group-0 binding-0 resource, defaulting to
// ctx.cameraUniformBuffer. One line in BatchManager.ts:
{ binding: 0, resource: { buffer: config.cameraBuffer || this.ctx.cameraUniformBuffer } }
```

`cameraBuffer` is what makes "a cascade is a camera" true end-to-end, and it is the enabling
change for every future off-main-view render: shadows, reflection probes, IBL capture, and any
editor picking pass. Without `depthOnly`, the §6.3 fallback renders with a throwaway `r8unorm`
color target at ~1.5–2× the pass cost (`allowColorFallback: true`).

---

## 8. Debugging checklist

| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| No shadow at all | `shadows.getPasses()` not spliced **before** the scene pass; or `update(camera)` not called this frame; or the light's `dir_rad` doesn't match `setLight` (the direction match is `> 0.999`). |
| Shadow acne (striped self-shadowing) | `constantBias` / `normalOffsetTexels` too low for the resolution, or a cascade too coarse for its extent. |
| Contact shadows detached (peter-panning) | `normalOffsetTexels × texelWorld` too large — the §11 guard throws at 2% of the extent. Raise `resolution` or lower `normalOffsetTexels`. |
| Shadows pop in as objects enter view | `casterExtrusion` too small — a caster behind the cascade was culled (§5.4). This is the most common CSM bug. |
| Shimmering / crawling edges as the camera moves | Texel snapping broken — `resolution` not a power of two, or the sphere fit re-quantized (§5.3/§5.5). |
| A visible seam between cascades | `blendTexels: 0` — the cross-fade band is what removes the resolution change (§8.3). |
| Bind-group creation throws on the caster | A declared-but-unused binding was pruned by `layout:'auto'` — the caster VS must reference both `camera` and `instances` (it does). |
| Everything past `shadowDistance` is dark | By design shadows stop at `shadowDistance` (not `camera.far`); raise it or shrink the cascade set. |

---
---

# Phase 2 — the atlas contract

Everything below applies when `atlasSize` is set. The Phase 1 layouts above (the cascade camera,
the caster params, the caster VS) are unchanged — the atlas *generalizes* the cascade into a
`ShadowView` plus an atlas rectangle, it does not replace the math.

## A1. The atlas + the view/slot tables

| Resource | Format / usage | Size |
|---|---|---|
| atlas | `depth24plus`, `RENDER_ATTACHMENT \| TEXTURE_BINDING` | `atlasSize²` (default 4096² ≈ 32 MB) |
| sampling view | `createView()` — plain `texture_depth_2d` | — |
| comparison sampler | `createSampler({ compare:'less', magFilter:'linear', minFilter:'linear' })` | — |
| `shadowViews` | `STORAGE`, `array<ShadowView>` | `96 × maxViews` |
| `shadowSlots` | `STORAGE`, `array<ShadowSlot>` | `16 × maxSlots` |
| per-view camera | `UNIFORM`, 432 B each | `432 × maxViews` |
| light-view Hi-Z | `HiZPyramid` over the atlas, `r32float` | `atlasSize² × 4/3` |

The two tables are `storage`, not `uniform`, so view and slot counts are **runtime values** and
the receiver shader is not recompiled when a light starts casting (§9.5).

### A1.1 `ShadowView` — 96 bytes (24 floats, 16-aligned)

What the *receiver* needs of a view. The CPU side additionally keeps the full 432-byte `Camera`
(§1.1) for the cull stage and the depth draw.

```wgsl
struct ShadowView {
    viewProj   : mat4x4<f32>,   // 64 B  world → this view's clip
    rect       : vec4<f32>,     // 16 B  atlas UV transform: .xy = uv scale, .zw = uv offset
    texelWorld : f32,           //       world size of one texel at the view's reference depth
    splitFar   : f32,           //       cascades: view-space depth covered; punctual: light range
    kind       : u32,           //       0 = cascade, 1 = spot, 2 = cube face
    _pad       : u32,           // 16 B
};                              // 96 B, 16-aligned
```

`rect` is the atlas's defining field: the tap offsets in the *view's* uv, clamps to `[0,1]²`, then
maps into the atlas via `local * rect.xy + rect.zw` — so a PCF tap can never read a neighbouring
light's depth (§9.4, pinned by U3).

### A1.2 `ShadowSlot` — 16 bytes (4 floats)

One per shadow-casting light. Directional lights own `cascadeCount` consecutive views, spots one,
points exactly six in `+X,−X,+Y,−Y,+Z,−Z` order so face selection is arithmetic (§9.2).

```wgsl
struct ShadowSlot {
    firstView  : u32,   // index into the views array
    viewCount  : u32,   // cascades: N; spot: 1; point: 6
    kind       : u32,   // 0 = directional, 1 = spot, 2 = point
    lightRange : f32,   // punctual only: for the depth remap at sample time
};
```

### A1.3 `ShadowParams` — 48 bytes (uniform, one per system)

Smaller than Phase 1's `ShadowData`: the per-cascade matrices and splits moved into the
`shadowViews` table, leaving only the global filter/bias knobs and the cascade split distances
(for `selectCascade`).

```wgsl
struct ShadowParams {
    atlasSize     : f32,          // atlas edge in px — texel = filterTexels / atlasSize
    pcfRadius     : u32,          // taps per side: 1 → 3×3, 2 → 5×5, 0 → hardware 2×2 only
    constantBias  : f32,
    filterTexels  : f32,          // PCF kernel width in texels (drives the tap step)
    cascadeSplits : vec4<f32>,    // view-space split far distances, up to MAX_CASCADES
    cascadeCount  : u32,
    _pad0         : f32,
    _pad1         : f32,
    _pad2         : f32,
};
```

## A2. The slot index on the light — `spot_params.z`

`spot_params.z` (float 14 of the 16-float light record) carries `slotIndex + 1`; `0` means "this
light does not cast." Free on **every** light type, requires no `LightSystem` edit, and the caller
sets it in the same `Float32Array` a worker already fills (`LightSystem.setRawData`):

```ts
const slot = shadows.registerLight({ kind: 'point', position, range: 30 });
lightData[lightIndex * 16 + 14] = slot + 1;      // spot_params.z
```

The Phase 1 `dot(dir, shadow.lightDir) > 0.999` heuristic is **deleted** in the atlas path, along
with its "two identical directional lights collide" caveat. Slots top out at 254 (the field
encodes `slot+1` as a float) — exceeding it throws the §11 error.

## A3. The receiver bindings (§9.5)

```wgsl
@group(3) @binding(0) var shadowAtlas   : texture_depth_2d;
@group(3) @binding(1) var shadowSampler : sampler_comparison;
@group(3) @binding(2) var<uniform> shadow : ShadowParams;
@group(3) @binding(3) var<storage, read> shadowViews : array<ShadowView>;
@group(3) @binding(4) var<storage, read> shadowSlots : array<ShadowSlot>;
```

## A4. The atlas decorator — slot → view → tap

The Phase 2 `getIncidentLight` keeps the decorator's shape; only the middle changes — the
direction match becomes a slot lookup, and the view choice becomes type-dependent:

```wgsl
fn getIncidentLight(i: u32, worldPos: vec3<f32>) -> IncidentLight {
    var inc = getIncidentLightUnshadowed(i, worldPos);
    let rec = ${accessor};                          // lights[i] | globalLights[lightIndices[...]]
    let packed = u32(rec.spot_params.z);            // 0 = no shadow, slot+1 otherwise
    if (packed == 0u) { return inc; }

    let slot = shadowSlots[packed - 1u];
    var v = slot.firstView;
    if (slot.kind == 0u) {                          // directional: pick the cascade
        let viewDepth = -(camera.view * vec4<f32>(worldPos, 1.0)).z;
        v = v + selectCascade(viewDepth);
    } else if (slot.kind == 2u) {                   // point: pick the cube face
        v = v + cubeFace(worldPos - rec.pos_type.xyz);
    }                                               // spot: the single view
    inc.attenuation = inc.attenuation * sampleView(v, worldPos);
    return inc;
}
```

`cubeFace` is the major-axis select matching the build order; `sampleView` is the atlas tap (§9.3)
with the tile clamp (§9.4). Both use `textureSampleCompareLevel` — never the bare form (the same
derivative-uniformity rule as Phase 1, §4).

## A5. The atlas pass + the tile clear

One depth-only pass holds every view's draws, each scoped to its tile by `PipelineConfig.viewport`
(§12.1). Caching needs `depthLoadOp: 'load'` on the atlas, so each dirty tile clears itself with a
`TILE_CLEAR_WGSL` batch — one full-viewport triangle at `z = 1.0`, `depthCompare: 'always'`,
scoped to the same viewport, drawn first (§8.2). Three vertices per dirty tile, no second pass.

```wgsl
@vertex
fn vs_main(@builtin(vertex_index) vi: u32) -> @builtin(position) vec4<f32> {
    var pos = array<vec2<f32>, 3>(vec2<f32>(-1.0, -1.0), vec2<f32>(3.0, -1.0), vec2<f32>(-1.0, 3.0));
    return vec4<f32>(pos[vi], 1.0, 1.0);
}
```

## A6. The visibility touchpoints (§12.2)

The atlas reuses the `VisibilitySystem` cull chain per view; two fields ride the existing
`CullParams` uniform (32 → 48 bytes):

```wgsl
struct CullParams {
    instanceCount : u32,
    meshIndex     : u32,
    hizMaxLevel   : u32,
    flags         : u32,
    screenSize    : vec2<f32>,
    lodErrorPx    : f32,
    _pad          : f32,
    hizRect       : vec4<f32>,   // NEW: .xy = uv scale, .zw = uv offset. Main view = (1,1,0,0).
};                               // 48 B
```

`occludedByHiZ` applies `hizRect` just before sampling, so a shadow view samples only its own
atlas tile. With `hizRect = (1,1,0,0)` the expression is the identity and the main view is
bit-for-bit unchanged (§10 U5). `screenSize` for a shadow view is the **tile** size, so the
footprint→mip selection stays correct. `HiZPyramid` itself is **unchanged** — it already accepts
an arbitrary depth view, so the light-view pyramid is built over last frame's atlas verbatim.

docs.title: Text API Usage
docs.text:
# Text API Usage

`null-graph/text` draws labels in the world — names over units, values over data points, signs on a
map — at object scale: **hundreds of thousands of labels in one draw call**, GPU-culled, crisp at
any size, fillable from a Worker, and able to follow positions only the GPU knows. Design:
[`text-labels-design.md`](../text-labels-design.md).

Labels are **screen-space**: a constant size in pixels, anchored to a world point, optionally
depth-tested at that point. UI and paragraphs stay in the DOM.

## 1. A font atlas

```ts
import { FontAtlas } from 'null-graph/text';

// Zero setup, browser or Worker: any font the browser can draw, distance-transformed now.
const atlas = FontAtlas.fromCanvas(engine, { fontFamily: 'Inter, sans-serif', fontWeight: 600 });

// Best quality: msdf-atlas-gen output (MSDF / MTSDF / SDF), e.g.
//   msdf-atlas-gen -font Inter.ttf -type msdf -size 48 -pxrange 6 -imageout inter.png -json inter.json
const img = await createImageBitmap(await (await fetch('inter.png')).blob(),
    { colorSpaceConversion: 'none', premultiplyAlpha: 'none' });   // the image is DATA, not colour
const msdf = FontAtlas.fromMSDF(engine, await (await fetch('inter.json')).json(), img);
```

`fromCanvas` needs `OffscreenCanvas`; in Node, load a pre-generated atlas with `fromMSDF` (pass raw
RGBA bytes as `{ data, width, height }`). The module ships no font data.

## 2. Labels

```ts
import { TextSystem } from 'null-graph/text';

const text = new TextSystem(engine, atlas, {
    maxLabels: 50_000,
    maxGlyphs: 500_000,
    depthTest: true,          // hide labels behind closer geometry (compared at the anchor)
    maxDistance: 400,         // cull labels farther than this from the eye
});
const batch = text.createDrawBatch(scenePass);          // put it LAST in its pass

text.setLabel(0, {
    text: 'Base Camp',
    position: [12, 4, -30],
    sizePx: 18,
    color: [1, 1, 1, 1],
    halo: { color: [0, 0, 0, 0.8], width: 2 },          // readable over anything
    offsetPx: [0, 12],                                  // nudge up 12 px on screen
    align: 'center', baseline: 'bottom',
});

// Per frame:
text.upload();                                          // dirty ranges only
engine.render([...vis.getComputeStages(), ...text.getComputeStages(), scenePass]);
```

Cheap updates without re-layout: `setLabelPosition(i, x, y, z)`, `setLabelHidden(i, hidden)`.
Layout options: `align` (`left`/`center`/`right`), `baseline` (`top`/`middle`/`alphabetic`/`bottom`),
`letterSpacing` and `maxWidth` (em, word wrap at spaces), `lineHeight` (multiple), `\n` for lines.

## 3. Labels that follow the GPU

Point labels at positions in any GPU buffer — the cull and draw read them there, so moving 50,000
agents costs the CPU nothing:

```ts
const text = new TextSystem(engine, atlas, {
    maxLabels: 50_000, maxGlyphs: 400_000,
    follow: { buffer: vis.instanceBuffer, strideFloats: 24, positionOffset: 12 },   // model translation
});
text.setLabel(i, { text: `unit ${i}`, follow: i, position: [0, 2.2, 0] });        // position = offset
```

## 4. From a Worker

`layoutText` is pure. Lay out in a Worker into flat records, transfer, adopt:

```ts
// worker
import { layoutText } from 'null-graph/text';
const n = layoutText(font, 'Hello', labelIndex, { align: 'center' }, glyphsU32, glyphsF32, offset).glyphs;

// main thread
text.setRawData(labelsF32, glyphsF32, glyphCount);     // adopted by reference; then text.upload()
```

`font` is anything implementing `LayoutFont` (glyph indices, advances, kerning, metrics) — a
`FontAtlas`, or a plain object built from the same atlas JSON. Records: label 12 floats
(`LABEL_FLOATS`), glyph 4 (`GLYPH_STRIDE`) — layouts in the design doc §4.

## 5. Notes

- **Scripts:** per-codepoint layout with kerning — Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, digits, CJK ideographs.
  No shaping, ligatures or right-to-left (Arabic, Devanagari… need a shaper).
- **Halos** are limited by the atlas's distance range: at most `distanceRange/2 · sizePx/emSize`
  pixels wide. Use a larger `distanceRange` (or an MTSDF atlas) for wide outlines.
- **Glyph capacity:** re-setting a label reuses its glyph range if the text fits, else takes a new
  range at the end. Give `maxGlyphs` headroom for labels whose text grows.
- One draw batch per `TextSystem` (it owns one cull). For a second view, use a second system.
- **Draw order inside a system is undefined.** The cull compacts visible glyphs with atomics, so
  overlapping labels blend in whatever order its threads finished. For labels that must read over
  the rest (a selection's details, a waypoint), give them a second small system with
  `depthTest: false`, created after the first so its batch draws later. Both systems can share
  one atlas and one follow buffer.
- **The depth test uses the anchor's depth across the whole quad.** A label drawn below a
  ground-level anchor (negative `offsetPx` y) sits over nearer ground and is hidden. Raise the
  anchor, offset upward, or use a `depthTest: false` system.
- **`destroy()`** releases the buffers and takes the batch out of its pass. Drop
  `getComputeStages()` from your sequence too.
- **Not yet:** decluttering (overlap removal), per-glyph colour, picking labels, world-size labels.

Executable reference: `test/text-gpu` (X1–X9 — position to the pixel, constant size, GPU cull = CPU
mirror, follow with zero CPU writes, depth test, halo, antialiasing, 600k glyphs in one draw).

docs.title: Time of Day API Usage
docs.text:
# Time of Day API Usage

`TimeOfDay` is the allocation-free celestial clock in `null-graph/environment`. It renders
nothing and owns no GPU resources. Its job is to compute the sun and moon once, then write the
same **travel directions** into the sky, directional lights, shadows, and exposure controls.

That removes a subtle but common failure mode: the sky highlight, direct light, and shadow camera
each being individually valid but pointed in different directions.

- **Environment and sky setup:** [`environment.md`](./environment.md)
- **Night sky and star catalogue:** [`night-sky.md`](./night-sky.md)
- **Physical atmosphere:** [`atmosphere.md`](./atmosphere.md)
- **Architecture and mechanics:**
  [`environment-timeofday-design.md`](../environment-timeofday-design.md)
- **Lights:** [`lights.md`](./lights.md)
- **Shadows:** [`shadows.md`](./shadows.md)
- **Post-processing:** [`post.md`](./post.md)

```ts
import {
    EnvironmentSystem, NightSky, PreethamSky, SkyComposite, StarField, TimeOfDay,
} from 'null-graph/environment';
import { DirectionalLightProxy, LightSystem } from 'null-graph/lights';
import { ShadowSystem } from 'null-graph/shadows';
import { AutoExposure, Tonemap } from 'null-graph/post';
```

---

## 1. Minimum animated-sky setup

Use analytic day/night `SkySource`s and an amortized environment. `TimeOfDay` changes source
parameters every frame, but requests expensive IBL work only after the sun or night-weighted moon
has moved by the configured angular threshold.

```ts
const env = new EnvironmentSystem(engine, {
    updateMode: 'amortized',
    keepSourceCube: true,
    prefilterMips: 6,
});

env.setSky(new SkyComposite({
    day: new PreethamSky({
        turbidity: 2.8,
        groundAlbedo: [0.15, 0.14, 0.12],
        sunAngularRadius: 0.266,
    }),
    night: new NightSky({ latitudeDeg: 45 }),
}));

const stars = new StarField(engine, { latitudeDeg: 45, maxStars: 9100 });

const tod = new TimeOfDay({
    mode: 'artistic',
    timeScale: 60,              // 60 simulated seconds per real second
    rebakeThresholdDeg: 0.25,
    exposureCoupling: 'off',    // no post effect is bound in this minimal example
    prefilterMips: 6,           // warning text only; match EnvironmentSystem
    purkinje: true,             // named artistic blue shift on the moon directional light
});

tod.setTime(8.0);               // 08:00 on the 0–24 artistic dial

const skyPass = env.getSkyPass({
    colorAttachments,
    depthStencilAttachment,
    size: [width, height],
    targetFormat: 'rgba16float',
});
stars.attach(env);              // append the unresolved-star batch after the resolved sky
```

Per frame:

```ts
function frame(dt: number) {
    tod.advance(dt);
    tod.applyTo({ environment: env, stars });

    // getBakeStages contains the declared-dirtiness gate and returns a shared empty array while
    // idle. During a trigger it emits one amortized slice per frame until every mip is refreshed.
    const bakeStages = env.getBakeStages();

    engine.render([
        ...bakeStages,
        ...vis.getComputeStages(),
        scenePass,
        skyPass,
        ...post.getPassSequence(),
    ]);

    if (bakeStages.length > 0) env.copySHToParams();
}
```

`copySHToParams()` must follow a submitted bake. The prefiltered cube is updated directly by the
compute stages, but diffuse IBL reads a separate uniform and needs this GPU-side copy.

### Why both dirty flags appear

- `tod.envDirty` becomes true when the maximum of solar motion and night-weighted lunar motion
  since the last published bake reaches `rebakeThresholdDeg`. Lunar motion is multiplied by
  `1 - dayFactor`, so a daytime moon does not force environment work.
- `env.bakeInvalidated` remains true until the environment has emitted all outstanding amortized
  mip slices. Repeated invalidations coalesce rather than restarting the cycle.

At the default threshold, real-time motion triggers roughly once per minute. A 1000× simulation
triggers around every four frames. A frame counter cannot behave correctly at both speeds.

`TimeOfDay` owns celestial invalidation only. If another source parameter changes—turbidity,
weather blend, or a custom sky parameter—upload that source state with `env.setSkyParams({})` and
call `env.invalidateBake()` yourself. The environment coalesces that request with any active
celestial refresh.

---

## 2. Driving directional lights

`TimeOfDay` writes through existing `DirectionalLightProxy` cursors. You own the light array, its
indices, and the eventual `LightSystem` upload.

```ts
const lights = new LightSystem(engine, {
    technique: 'clustered-forward',
    capacity: { point: 32, directional: 2, spot: 8 },
    clusterConfig: { grid: [16, 9, 24], maxLightsPerTile: 32 },
});

const lightData = new Float32Array(
    (32 + 2 + 8) * LightSystem.FLOATS_PER_LIGHT,
);

const sun = new DirectionalLightProxy();
sun.wrap(lightData);
sun.seek(32);                    // index ownership remains yours

const moon = new DirectionalLightProxy();
moon.wrap(lightData);
moon.seek(33);

lights.setRawData(lightData);    // adopts the same array by reference
```

Then update and upload:

```ts
tod.advance(dt);
tod.applyTo({ environment: env, sun, moon });
lights.setRawData(lightData);    // marks the adopted array dirty
lights.upload();
```

The clock writes:

- normalized travel direction to both records;
- extinction-attenuated linear HDR colour;
- a sun intensity that is zero at and below geometric sunset;
- moon colour scaled by phase illumination, with intensity disabled below the horizon;
- a named optional Purkinje weighting on the moon light (`purkinje: true` by default).

If you do not want a moon light, omit `moon`. Lunar direction, phase, and illumination still drive
`NightSky` when the environment binding is present.

### Moonlight colour and `purkinje`

The moon's radiometric weighting is slightly warm. The familiar blue moonlit look is an observer
effect, not blue illumination, so it is exposed as a named artistic option:

```ts
const cinematic = new TimeOfDay({ purkinje: true });   // default: blue-biased moon light
const radiometric = new TimeOfDay({ purkinje: false }); // warm moon light weighting
```

This changes the directional moon light written to `DirectionalLightProxy`; it does not recolour
the lunar disc in `NightSky`.

---

## 3. Shadows and the sun/moon handoff

The current `ShadowSystem` has one directional shadow direction. Sun and moon therefore share one
registered directional atlas slot, and exactly one light record may hold it at a time.

At setup time, on the atlas shadow path:

```ts
const celestialShadowSlot = shadows.registerLight({
    kind: 'directional',
    name: 'sun-or-moon',
});
```

Per frame:

```ts
tod.applyTo({
    environment: env,
    sun,
    moon,
    shadows,
    shadowSlot: celestialShadowSlot,
});
```

`applyTo()` performs the related writes together:

1. removes the slot from the inactive light;
2. assigns it to the active light, if any;
3. updates the shadow direction and registered atlas light;
4. invalidates the slot's cached views.

The default handoff rules are:

- sun casts at elevations of at least `3°`;
- moon casts at elevations of at least `10°` and illumination of at least `0.35`;
- otherwise `activeBody` is `'none'` and neither record owns the slot.

The gap is intentional. Directional shadow depth precision degrades near the horizon, and a true
sun/moon shadow crossfade would require two live cascade sets.

Without the atlas path, passing `shadows` still drives `ShadowSystem.setLight()`. Omit
`shadowSlot`; registered-slot updates and invalidation apply only when an atlas slot is supplied.

---

## 4. Exposure coupling

Exposure coupling is explicit. `TimeOfDay` does not search a `PostChain` because the chain keeps
effect ownership private; pass the effect instance you already placed in the chain.

### Histogram adaptation with a day/night clamp

This is the default mode:

```ts
const autoExposure = new AutoExposure();

const tod = new TimeOfDay({
    exposureCoupling: 'clamp',
});

tod.applyTo({ environment: env, sun, moon, autoExposure });
```

`'clamp'` changes `AutoExposure.minExposure` and `maxExposure` from `dayFactor`; the existing
histogram and temporal adaptation remain authoritative inside that window. Omitting
`autoExposure` in this mode throws.

### Deterministic exposure

```ts
const tonemap = new Tonemap({ curve: 'aces' });
const tod = new TimeOfDay({ exposureCoupling: 'absolute' });

tod.applyTo({ environment: env, sun, moon, tonemap });
```

`'absolute'` drives `Tonemap.exposure` directly from `dayFactor`. Omitting `tonemap` throws.

### No clock-owned exposure

```ts
const tod = new TimeOfDay({ exposureCoupling: 'off' });
```

Use `'off'` when the application already owns exposure or when no post chain is present.

---

## 5. Clock modes

### Artistic mode — default

```ts
const tod = new TimeOfDay({
    mode: 'artistic',
    sunTiltDeg: 23.44,
    date: new Date('2026-06-21T00:00:00Z'),
});

tod.setTime(18.5);               // 18:30
```

The visible sun follows a geography-free great circle. Noon is the top of the arc; 06:00 and
18:00 touch the geometric horizon. The date still drives the real lunar phase and GMST used by
`NightSky` and `StarField`.

### Astronomical mode

```ts
const tod = new TimeOfDay({
    mode: 'astronomical',
    latitudeDeg: 51.5074,
    longitudeDeg: -0.1278,       // east-positive, west-negative
    date: new Date('2026-06-21T00:00:00Z'),
    timeScale: 600,
});
```

Astronomical mode uses the configured UTC date and time, latitude, and longitude. It includes
seasonal day length and polar day/night. Both coordinates are required; use artistic mode if you
do not want geography.

`advance(dt)` takes **real seconds** and applies `timeScale`. `setTime(hours)` sets the current
UTC/artistic 0–24 time while retaining the configured date.

---

## 6. Configuration reference

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `mode` | `'artistic'` | `'artistic'` or `'astronomical'`. |
| `latitudeDeg` | `45` | Observer latitude. Required explicitly in astronomical mode. |
| `longitudeDeg` | `0` | Observer longitude, east-positive. Required explicitly in astronomical mode. |
| `date` | current date/time | Initial UTC date and 0–24 time. Converted to Julian day at construction. |
| `sunTiltDeg` | `23.44` | Artistic great-circle tilt. |
| `timeScale` | `1` | Simulated seconds per real second. |
| `rebakeThresholdDeg` | `0.25` | Maximum solar/night-weighted lunar angular motion required to invalidate IBL. Must be greater than zero. |
| `sunShadowMinElevDeg` | `3` | Minimum sun elevation for shadow ownership. |
| `moonShadowMinElevDeg` | `10` | Minimum moon elevation for shadow ownership. |
| `moonMinIllumination` | `0.35` | Minimum illuminated fraction for moon shadows. |
| `civilDeg` | `-6` | Elevation at which `dayFactor` reaches 1. |
| `nightDeg` | `-18` | Elevation at which `dayFactor` reaches 0. Must be below `civilDeg`. |
| `exposureCoupling` | `'clamp'` | `'off'`, `'clamp'`, or `'absolute'`. |
| `turbidity` | `2.8` | Turbidity used by the CPU sun/moon radiance mirror. Match `PreethamSky`. |
| `prefilterMips` | `6` | Used only in the warning for a re-bake threshold above `2°`; match the environment. |
| `purkinje` | `true` | Apply the named artistic blue shift to the directional moon light. |

`rebakeThresholdDeg > 2` is legal but warns: an amortized cube is mixed-age for several frames,
which can make rough reflections step visibly.

---

## 7. Runtime API

### Methods

| Method | Notes |
|---|---|
| `setTime(hours)` | Set the wrapped 0–24 time and recompute state. |
| `advance(dtSeconds)` | Advance by real seconds multiplied by `timeScale`, then recompute. |
| `update()` | Recompute without advancing. Normally called indirectly by the two methods above. |
| `applyTo(bindings)` | Write all supplied consumers. The caller still uploads the light array. |
| `getSunDirection(out?)` | Return the persistent internal view, or fill and return `out`. |
| `getMoonDirection(out?)` | Return the persistent internal view, or fill and return `out`. |

The no-argument direction views are valid until the next `update()`, `advance()`, or `setTime()`.
Use an `out` array when the value must be retained independently.

### Read-only state

| Property | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `envDirty` | Solar or night-weighted lunar motion reached the IBL re-bake threshold this update. |
| `activeBody` | `'sun'`, `'moon'`, or `'none'` for directional shadow ownership. |
| `dayFactor` | Smooth twilight factor: 0 at/below `nightDeg`, 1 at/above `civilDeg`. |
| `sunElevationDeg` | Solar elevation above the horizon. |
| `moonElevationDeg` | Lunar elevation above the horizon. |
| `moonPhase` | Wrapped phase: 0 new, 0.5 full. |
| `moonIllumination` | Illuminated fraction in `[0, 1]`. |
| `gmstRad` | Greenwich mean sidereal time used to rotate `NightSky` and `StarField`. |

### `TimeOfDayBindings`

Every binding is optional, but the selected exposure mode may require its corresponding effect.

| Field | Written by `applyTo()` |
|---|---|
| `environment` | Full celestial state (`sunDir`, `moonDir`, illumination, GMST, `dayFactor`), source params, and bake invalidation. |
| `stars` | GMST through `setCelestialState`, followed by `StarField.upload()`. |
| `sun` | Direction, colour, intensity, and shadow slot. |
| `moon` | Direction, colour, intensity, and shadow slot. |
| `shadows` | Active directional shadow direction and atlas record/cache. |
| `shadowSlot` | Shared registered directional atlas slot. |
| `autoExposure` | Clamp pair in `'clamp'` mode. |
| `tonemap` | Exposure in `'absolute'` mode. |

---

## 8. Pure celestial helpers

`todMath` is exported from `null-graph/environment` and has no GPU or browser dependency:

```ts
import {
    createSolarPosition,
    julianDay,
    solarPosition,
} from 'null-graph/environment';

const out = createSolarPosition();             // allocate once
const jd = julianDay(new Date());

solarPosition(jd, 45, 0, out);                 // reuses out
console.log(out.elevationDeg, out.azimuthDeg, out.direction);
```

Exported helpers include `julianDay`, `gmstRadians`, `solarPosition`,
`artisticSolarPosition`, `lunarPosition`, `skySunRadiance`, `sunIntensity`, and
`angularDistanceDeg`. `createSolarPosition()` and `createLunarPosition()` create reusable output
records; omitting `out` from a position helper allocates for one-shot use.

Phase 3's pure catalogue and lunar helpers live in `nightMath`; see
[`night-sky.md`](./night-sky.md) §7.

---

## 9. Errors and warnings

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| Astronomical mode without both coordinates | Throws, naming artistic mode as the geography-free alternative. |
| Latitude outside `[-90, 90]` | Throws with the supplied value. |
| `rebakeThresholdDeg <= 0` | Throws; zero is equivalent to unconditional amortized work. |
| Moon shadow elevation below the sun threshold | Throws because the eligibility windows overlap. |
| `nightDeg >= civilDeg` | Throws because the twilight ramp would be empty or inverted. |
| Clamp coupling without `AutoExposure` | Throws and suggests absolute coupling. |
| Absolute coupling without `Tonemap` | Throws and names the missing effect. |
| `rebakeThresholdDeg > 2` | Warns about mixed-age prefilter mips and visible reflection stepping. |

---

## 10. Testing

```bash
npm run test:tod
```

The headless suite covers solar symmetry, the physical transmittance radiance mirror, polar
day/night, exclusive
shadow-slot ownership, handoff call order, sunset intensity, the re-bake gate at 1× and 1000×,
lunar phase/illumination, normalized directions, zero typed-array allocation over 1,000 frame
updates, `out` semantics, and configuration errors. It needs no GPU, device, or browser.

Phase 3's transform, lunar-disc, star-flux, composite, and generated-WGSL checks are in:

```bash
npm run test:night
```

It is also included in:

```bash
npm run test:environment
```

docs.title: Visibility API Usage
docs.text:
# Visibility API Usage

The `null-graph/visibility` module is the GPU-driven culling runtime. It decides **on the GPU**
what to draw — frustum, meshlet normal-cone (backface cluster), and Hi-Z occlusion culling, plus
LOD selection — and issues the draws indirectly, so the CPU never iterates the scene. Draw-call
count becomes proportional to material/mesh count, not instance count.

It is a batteries-included wrapper over the engine's existing indirect-draw primitive
(`createBatch({ isIndirect: true })` + `drawIndexedIndirect`), consuming the meshlet buffers
produced by [`MeshletBuilder`](./geometry.md#meshletbuilder-v105).

- **Architecture:** [`visibility-design.md`](../visibility-design.md)
- **Buffer layouts, WGSL contracts, material bridge:** [`visibility-shader-reference.md`](./visibility-shader-reference.md)

```ts
import {
    VisibilitySystem, InstanceBuffer, LOD_AUTO,
    INSTANCE_FLAG_NO_OCCLUSION, INSTANCE_FLAG_NO_CONE_CULL,
} from 'null-graph/visibility';
import { MegabufferBuilder, MeshletBuilder } from 'null-graph/geometry';
```

---

## Do you need this?

| Scene | Use |
|---|---|
| A few dozen objects | **Not this.** Plain `engine.createBatch` is simpler and just as fast. |
| Thousands of instances of a few meshes | **Instance tier** — the big win, and it needs no meshlets. |
| Huge meshes (100k+ tris) mostly off-screen or back-facing | **Meshlet tier** — sub-object culling. |
| Dense occlusion (interiors, cities) | Add **Hi-Z** on either tier. |

Visibility trades setup complexity for scene-size independence. Below a few hundred objects that
trade is not worth it.

## Two tiers

| Tier | Granularity | Draw calls | Needs meshlets? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Instance** | per-object | one per unique mesh | no — `setGeometry(mega)` alone |
| **Meshlet** | per-cluster (≤64v/≤124t) | one per material | yes — `setGeometry(mega, pack)` |

Both share one mega vertex pool, one Hi-Z pyramid, and the indirect-draw mechanism. Pick per draw
batch; you can mix them in one scene.

---

## 1. Build geometry

`MeshletBuilder` layers on `MegabufferBuilder` — one unified vertex pool backs both tiers.

```ts
const mega = new MegabufferBuilder(8);                  // 8 floats/vertex: pos(3) normal(3) uv(2)
const meshlets = new MeshletBuilder(mega, { positionOffsetFloats: 0, normalOffsetFloats: 3 });

const rock = meshlets.addMesh('rock', { vertices: rockVerts, indices: rockIndices });
const tree = meshlets.addMesh('tree', {
    vertices: treeVerts,
    lods: [                                             // optional discrete LOD chain
        { indices: treeLOD0, error: 0.0  },
        { indices: treeLOD1, error: 0.05 },             // world-space geometric error
        { indices: treeLOD2, error: 0.20 },
    ],
});

const pack = meshlets.build();                          // omit if you only want the instance tier
```

For the instance tier alone, a plain `MegabufferBuilder` (no `MeshletBuilder`) is enough.

## 2. Create the system

```ts
const vis = new VisibilitySystem(engine, {
    maxInstances: 100_000,                  // sizes the instance + work buffers

    // meshlet tier only:
    maxMeshletsPerInstance: 256,            // max meshlets in any one LOD
    maxVisibleMeshletInstances: 2_000_000,  // per-frame visible-cluster budget

    // optional Hi-Z occlusion — needs a SAMPLABLE depth view (not ctx.depthTexture):
    // hiZ: { depthSource: myDepthView },

    lodErrorPx: 1.0,                        // screen-space error budget (default 1.0)
});

vis.setGeometry(mega, pack);                // pack optional → instance tier only
```

| Option | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `maxInstances` | — | Required, ≥ 1. |
| `maxMeshletsPerInstance` | — | Required for the meshlet tier. |
| `maxVisibleMeshletInstances` | — | Required for the meshlet tier. Too small ⇒ flicker; see the debug table in the shader reference. |
| `hiZ` | off | Omit for frustum + cone culling only. |
| `lodErrorPx` | `1.0` | Larger ⇒ coarser LODs sooner. |
| `mode` | `'single-phase'` | `'two-phase'` is reserved and **throws**. |

## Model-space vertex hooks (instance tier)

`createInstanceDrawBatch` accepts `vertexHook: { wgsl, bindings, entries, group?, instanceIndex? }`.
The generated vertex stage calls your function before the instance model transform:
`fn deform(pos: vec3<f32>, normal: vec3<f32>, vi: u32, inst: Instance) -> Deformed`.
Visibility supplies `struct Deformed { position: vec3<f32>, normal: vec3<f32> }`.
Set `instanceIndex: true` to opt in to a fifth `slot: u32` argument after `inst`: the compacted
`@builtin(instance_index)` of this draw. Use it to read a palette produced over this batch's visible
list after culling. It differs from `inst.sourceIndex`, the original simulation row. Existing hooks
remain four-argument by default. See the loaders guide's visible-model palette section.
Return both values in model space; visibility then applies the instance model matrix and its
inverse-transpose normal matrix. UVs and the stock material fragment contract are unchanged.

This complete batch-registration example type-checks and runs in `npm run test:visibility`:

```ts
import type { RenderPassNode } from 'null-graph';
import { VisibilitySystem } from 'null-graph/visibility';

// offsets is STORAGE: one vec4<f32> per source row, xyz = model-space displacement.
export function addDeformedBatch(vis: VisibilitySystem, pass: RenderPassNode,
    meshName: string, meshIndex: number, offsets: GPUBuffer) {
    return vis.createInstanceDrawBatch(pass, meshName, meshIndex, {
        vertexHook: {
            group: 2,
            bindings: '@group(2) @binding(0) var<storage, read> offsets: array<vec4<f32>>;',
            entries: [{ binding: 0, resource: { buffer: offsets } }],
            wgsl: `fn deform(pos: vec3<f32>, normal: vec3<f32>, vi: u32, inst: Instance) -> Deformed {
                return Deformed(pos + offsets[inst.sourceIndex].xyz, normal);
            }`,
        },
    });
}
```

- **`vi` is absolute:** indexed draws include the mesh's `baseVertex`. Per-vertex storage
  (such as `bakeRigidAnimation().partOfVertex`) must be padded/placed at that mesh's offset in
  the whole mega vertex pool, not indexed from zero for every mesh.
- **`inst.sourceIndex` is the original row**, not the compacted visible-list index. Agents use
  `sourceIndex - firstInstance` to address their own record. The instance tier writes survivors in
  ascending source order (visibility-design §14), but `slot` still shifts as instances enter and
  leave the view.
- **Bindings use a dedicated group**, default **2**. Their WGSL is emitted verbatim: `group`
  chooses where `entries` bind, it does not rewrite declarations. Group 0 is engine-owned.
  Choose group 3 (and declare `@group(3)`) when clustered lighting uses 2; stock materials
  normally use 1. Other lighting/environment bindings can occupy further groups: check your
  layout and `device.limits.maxBindGroups`. Numeric group collisions with generated material
  or extra bindings are refused. Keep group attributes literal and do not hide declarations
  behind WGSL constant expressions. Unoccupied intervening groups are bound empty automatically.
- **Composition:** works with `material`, `fragmentBody`, `extraBindings` and custom vertex
  attributes named `pos`, `normal`, `uv`. A full `shaderCode` override plus a hook is refused;
  use one or the other. Meshlet draws do not support the hook.
- **Bounds and passes:** culling and picking are not deformed. Supply a sphere covering all
  displayed poses (the rigid bake reports one). Shadow caster passes need matching deformation
  in their own vertex stage; hooks are not automatically propagated to `ShadowSystem`.
- **Ownership:** buffers stay caller-owned. Update them through the queue or compute stages
  before drawing; keep them alive until all batches using them have been removed. The hook
  adds no per-instance CPU updates or new vertex attributes.

For baked rigid animation, upload the part indices and 3×4 transform rows once, select a frame
from each source row's animation state, and apply its part's rows in `deform`. Transform normals
with the inverse transpose of that part transform when scaling is non-uniform. See the
[loaders guide](./loaders.md#baked-rigid-animation-many-instances-one-shared-table) for packing
and sampling. With no hook, generated instance draw WGSL is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## 3. Fill instances (zero-copy, worker-fillable)

Instances are 96 bytes each (24 floats): a column-major model matrix, an object-space bounding
sphere, and the mesh reference. Adopt the array by reference — nothing is copied until `upload()`.

```ts
const instances = new InstanceBuffer(100_000);
instances.write(
    i,
    modelMat4,                  // column-major 16 floats (gl-matrix mat4)
    [cx, cy, cz, radius],       // object-space bounding sphere
    rock.meshIndex,
    LOD_AUTO,                   // or a relative level: 0 = finest
    0,                          // flags
);
```

`flags` bits: `INSTANCE_FLAG_NO_OCCLUSION` (skip Hi-Z for this instance — useful for the object the
camera is inside), `INSTANCE_FLAG_NO_CONE_CULL` (skip backface cluster rejection — for two-sided
foliage).

A Web Worker can fill the raw arrays directly; the exact byte layout is in the
[shader reference §1.1](./visibility-shader-reference.md#11-instance--96-bytes-24-floats).

**The bounding sphere must enclose the mesh.** A too-small radius culls geometry that is actually
visible — the most common source of "things pop out at the screen edge."

### Rows written on the GPU

When a compute stage writes the rows itself (an agent system, a particle simulation), there is no
CPU array to adopt. Set the count instead:

```ts
vis.setInstanceCount(n);   // the culls dispatch over n rows; upload() now writes only cull params
// Rows that never move can share the system: write them once, nothing overwrites them.
device.queue.writeBuffer(vis.instanceBuffer, 0, props.data);
```

`vis.instanceSource` reads `'gpu'` after `setInstanceCount()` and `'cpu'` otherwise. A later
`setInstances(data, count)` adopts an array again, and `upload()` resumes copying it every frame.
Splice the stage that writes the rows **before** `vis.getComputeStages()`, so the culls read this
frame's rows.

## 4. Register draw batches

One per unique mesh (instance tier) or per material (meshlet tier).

```ts
// Instance tier — one draw call for all rocks, regardless of count:
const rockBatch = vis.createInstanceDrawBatch(scenePass, 'rock', rock.meshIndex, {
    vertexLayouts: StandardLayout.getWebGPUDescriptor(),
});

// Meshlet tier — one draw call covering every meshlet of every instance:
const meshletBatch = vis.createMeshletDrawBatch(scenePass, { /* material options */ });
```

Both accept `fragmentBody`, `extraBindings`, `materialEntries`, `materialGroupIndex`, and
`targetFormat`. The default fragment is a neutral hemispheric shade — good for bring-up, not for
real rendering. See §6.

> **`fragmentBody` is a whole entry point, not a body.** Supply the complete function —
> `@fragment fn fs_main(in: VertexOut) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> { … }` — where `VertexOut` carries
> `clipPos`, `worldPos`, `worldNormal`, `uv` and `ecsColor`. A bare `return …;` is a WGSL parse
> error ("statement found outside of function body").

**Which instance am I?** The instance cull copies survivors into a compacted list, and writes each
one's index in your `InstanceBuffer` into the record's last field — `sourceIndex` in WGSL,
`INSTANCE_SOURCE_INDEX_OFFSET` (= 23) on the CPU. A custom instance-tier shader reads
`instances[instance_index].sourceIndex` to look up per-instance data the record does not hold;
picking uses it to report your index. The compacted list is in **ascending source order**, the same
every frame and every run. So the draw order is stable, and overlapping instances do not trade depth
ties between frames (visibility-design §14; the meshlet tier's order is not defined yet).
**`vis.instanceBuffer`** is public (read-only): the GPU copy
of your records, for other GPU consumers — e.g. labels that follow instances
(`TextSystem` `follow: { buffer: vis.instanceBuffer, strideFloats: 24, positionOffset: 12 }`).

A batch's parameters are written when it is registered, so a batch created after this frame's
`upload()` still draws on its first frame. To tear one down — a system you destroy while the
`VisibilitySystem` it shares lives on — call `vis.removeDrawBatch(batch)`: its cull stage leaves
the chain, its params buffer is released, and the batch leaves its pass. (A cull stage that outlives
its owner keeps binding the owner's destroyed buffers, and every later frame is refused at submit;
`ShadowSystem.destroy()` does this for its casters.)

### Level of detail by size on screen (instance tier)

A batch can draw its mesh index's rows only while they look large enough, or small enough. Two
batches over the **same mesh index** with adjoining bands draw every row exactly once: as the full
mesh near the camera and as a stand-in far away. The size is the diameter of the row's bounding
sphere in pixels, measured as the meshlet tier's LOD measures it (nearest distance, vertical field
of view, screen height). It is checked in each batch's own cull, one comparison per row; a batch
without `lod` culls exactly as before.

